The gantry head travels on two Linear Guides (profile rails): a carriage block rides a hardened rail on recirculating balls, so it rolls instead of sliding and keeps the cutter square. Broach one Bearing Steel Stock in the Broach Press to cut its two ball tracks (Guide Rail Blank), then harden the blank in the Quench Vat with 250 mB water (160 ticks, 12 FE/t). Craft the guide with a Tempered Steel carriage on top, two Bearing Balls either side of the Hardened Guide Rail, and a Pressure Gasket below as the end seal wiper. An unhardened blank, an iron block or a sintered bushing (a sliding guide) does not fit. Bearing Steel comes from the Kiln and the balls from the Pressure Press, both before this tier. The vat is hopper- and pipe-fed, so rails can be hardened automatically; broaching is hand-fed.

The Spindle Gearbox steps the motion down so the mill head turns slowly with high torque. Gears are made in two steps, like real powder-metal gears: the Pressure Press compacts 3 Bronze Powder Blend into a fragile Green Gear Compact (100 ticks, 6 FE/t), then the Copper Hot Press sinters that compact into a Sintered Bronze Gear (160 ticks, 10 FE/t). Pressed-and-sintered bronze suits slow, lightly loaded gearing like this; hardened steel gears come later. Broach one Tool Steel Stock in the Broach Press for two rectangular Shaft Keys; one locks the hub to the Drive Shaft so torque reaches the cutter instead of the gear slipping. A round Broached Pin cannot transfer torque across this keyed hub. Put one key at the gearbox bottom-left, two gears either side of a Sealed Steel Plate housing on top, a Hydrodynamic Journal Bearing either side of the Drive Shaft, and one Lubricating Oil in the bottom centre. Press 8 forge:seeds in the Pressure Press for 160 ticks at 10 FE/t per oil. The oil bath splashes over the gears; Bearing Grease cannot replace it. Each journal bearing uses two Sintered Bronze Bushings, two forge:ingots/copper and one pressed Lubricating Oil in a crafting grid. Feed 3 Bronze Powder Blend into the Copper Hot Press for each bushing (120 ticks, 10 FE/t); its porous bronze sleeve holds oil at the rotating shaft while the copper end collars retain it. A loose dry bushing cannot replace the assembled bearing. Oil-film pressure, supply plumbing and wear are abstracted, so this is not a simulated fluid bearing. Hopper blend and seeds into their presses, extract outputs below, and automate the final grid crafts with ordinary crafting equipment. A bare plate or loose Drive Shaft cannot replace the gearbox.

Right-click the controller with feedstock from a loaded milling recipe. One complete batch of that recipe's input count loads into the controller; after 40 ticks, right-click with an empty hand to collect the output. A busy controller refuses another batch without consuming it. Missing or outward-facing pistons, anvil or redstone stop operation. One Tool Steel Stock mills into two Governor Flyweights, the balanced bobs of the Corona Collector's Flyweight Governor. Recovery never exceeds the craft cost: one mud bricks block returns one packed mud, and one purpur block returns one popped chorus fruit.

It runs 22 exclusive datapack milling recipes. Four glass panes give optic powder for the Heliostat Etcher; batches of andesite, diorite and granite yield gravel, while calcite yields sand. Sandstone and smooth sandstone recover sand; their red variants recover red sand. Quartz, purpur, bone, amethyst, brick, mud brick and nether brick blocks recover their component materials. Prismarine variants recover shards (prismarine and prismarine bricks each return four), and dripstone blocks recover pointed dripstone. These are separate inputs with distinct recovery paths rather than duplicate color recipes. JEI's Milling category lists loaded input counts and outputs; click the Milling Gantry catalyst to browse them. The gantry accepts hand-fed stock: hold the listed input count and right-click a formed controller to load one timed batch. For automation, insert valid milling stock into the controller from any face except the bottom and extract products from the bottom; reach these covered faces through Stock Hatches. Each formed batch takes 40 ticks; breaking the structure pauses processing without consuming stock. The controller buffers one input stack and one output stack, saves both and its face modes, and exposes Forge item handlers to hoppers or pipes. Sneak-right-click with an empty hand to cycle the clicked face through input, output and disabled; right-click with an empty hand to collect buffered output. It has no FE port.

The Power Contactor needs one Stamped Contactor Enclosure in its bottom-left craft slot. Make it from two Sealed Steel Plates in the Pressure Press for 140 ticks at 10 FE/t; three remaining plates brace the corners. The stamped box protects the busbar, wound coils and Limit Switch from exposed debris. Loose plates cannot replace the enclosure. Transfer the press output into the contactor grid, then use that contactor at the Milling Gantry top centre. Contact separation and ingress protection are represented by the part rather than simulated.

Stock Hatches: every face of this controller is covered by a frame part, so hoppers and pipes reach it through Stock Hatches. Place a hatch instead of any part that touches the controller face-to-face; at most two hatches may stand in, and a third breaks formation. A hatch relays only while the frame is formed, and it relays the controller face it covers: insert stock into a hatch on an In face, and extract products from a hatch whose face you sneak-use with an empty hand to cycle to Out (the base face starts as Out). For example, swap one side part for a hatch fed by a hopper pointing into it from beside, and swap the base part for a hatch with a hopper beneath it. A hopper touching a redstone block or other powered part is locked by vanilla rules. Right-clicking a hatch with an empty hand collects the product buffer.
guide.arcana_industry.ash_bellows.page1: Build ash bellows from four leather, one milled dowel, one stick, two iron ingots and a brick. Crafting rows: leather/milled-dowel/leather; iron/brick/iron; leather/stick/leather. Mine it with a stone pickaxe or better. This is a fifth t0 apparatus alongside the crusher, sieve, refractory mixer and quern, but unlike the quern its output is a required kiln ingredient. The milled dowel corner requires a sawmill, so build one first and feed it any log or a plain stick.
guide.arcana_industry.ash_bellows.page2: Right-click to open the bellows. It reuses the crusher's menu layout: place fuel in the left slot, collect ash from the right slot, Crank supplies 80 FE, and six buttons cycle each world face through Off, In and Out exactly like the crusher, sieve and quern.
guide.arcana_industry.ash_bellows.page3: Twenty-seven datapack ashing recipes run in this bellows. Charcoal or coal make Temper Ash for the kiln. Logs and stems char into fuel, while kelp dries and other combustible materials yield useful ash-processing products. Distinct bulk heat jobs turn sand into glass, cobblestone into stone, netherrack into nether brick, and a clay block into four bricks. Four clay balls fire into one terracotta block; crushing it recovers four balls. TNT yields five gunpowder, equal to the five spent by the Containment Forge or Stasis Weaver to make one TNT. Sea pickles yield lime dye and cocoa beans yield brown dye. Bulk loads beat a furnace or crafting grid: four netherrack, sea pickles, cocoa beans or kelp give five products, and four blaze rods give ten powder. Each uses 4 FE per tick; load one input at a time.
guide.arcana_industry.ash_bellows.page4: Temper ash replaces one of the kiln's three copper grit slots: the kiln now needs bricks, a refractory binder, a furnace, screened flux, copper grit and temper ash together, so the ash bellows is progression-required from t0 onward, not a parallel side process like the quern.
guide.arcana_industry.ash_bellows.page5: Automation: side ports, energy handling, NBT persistence and hopper behavior are identical to the crusher, sieve and quern. Charcoal farms and log-processing lines gain a mechanized destination that feeds kiln construction directly.
guide.arcana_industry.ash_bellows.page6: Recipes are datapack JSON under data/<namespace>/recipes/ashing. Type: arcana_industry:ashing. Fields: ingredient (item or tag), count (default 1), result (item/count), duration (1-72000 ticks), energy_per_tick (1-1000), priority (default 0). Highest priority wins; equal priorities use ascending recipe ID.
guide.arcana_industry.ash_bellows.page7: With Just Enough Items installed, click the progress strip to browse Ashing recipes, or look up an ingredient or product in JEI. The ash bellows is the category catalyst. JEI is optional; all processing and this guide work without it.
guide.arcana_industry.ember_dryer.page1: Craft the Ember Dryer from two plain brick blocks, one Carbon Brick from the Char Retort, one Clinker Brick from the Clinker Oven, a copper ingot, two iron bars, a furnace and redstone. The Carbon Brick occupies the upper-left corner and the Clinker Brick the upper-right corner; plain bricks in either corner do not work. Build the Char Retort and the Clinker Oven (each needs a Kiln) first. Dry one nether-brick block to make a Cured Hearth Brick; place it in the Soaking Hearth craft's upper-left corner.
guide.arcana_industry.ember_dryer.page2: Feed the ingredient stack into the left slot: four kelp, sugar cane, cactus, sea pickles, chorus fruit or raw meat and fish dry into five results, while potatoes, clay, sponges and the other jobs use one input. The dryer spends 8 FE/t for 80 ticks and places the result in the right slot. Twenty exclusive recipes dry kelp, sponge, clay, chorus fruit, foods and pigments. JEI displays the input, output and FE. Datapack type arcana_industry:drying accepts ingredient, count, result, duration, energy_per_tick and optional priority; higher priority wins, then recipe ID.
guide.arcana_industry.ember_dryer.page3: Top and horizontal sides import; the bottom exports. Side buttons change each face between input, output and disabled. Supply FE by capability or the manual crank. The dryer pauses on a full output slot. Inventory, FE, work progress and side modes persist across saves; breaking it drops both slots.
guide.arcana_industry.smoke_rack.page1: Craft the rack controller from a sealed steel plate, oak fences and iron bars. Place it above a lit campfire. Add oak fences on the north, east and west sides, raise the south fence one block above the controller, and place iron bars at all four same-level corners. The open south face accepts an output pipe.
guide.arcana_industry.smoke_rack.page2: Right-click the formed controller with four complete batches of an arcana_industry:rack_smoking recipe to load the stock buffer. A lit, formed rack smokes the batch over 40 ticks; empty-hand use collects the finished output. A short batch or full buffer leaves held items untouched. Missing braces, fences or heat pause processing.
guide.arcana_industry.smoke_rack.page3: Twenty-one exclusive rack recipes dry and fire common materials. The original ten cover cactus to green dye, clay to brick or terracotta, cobblestone to stone, sand to glass, oak logs to charcoal, wet sponge to sponge, netherrack to nether brick, chorus fruit to popped chorus fruit, and sea pickles to lime dye. Other mods' campfire recipes do not run on the rack.
guide.arcana_industry.smoke_rack.page4: Additional batches fire red sand to glass, stone to smooth stone, sandstone to smooth sandstone, red sandstone to smooth red sandstone, basalt to smooth basalt, cobbled deepslate to deepslate, and blackstone to polished blackstone. These offer hand-fed alternatives to furnaces and the Blast Column. Batch yields beat the furnace where nothing can turn the product back: four basalt, blackstone, stone, red sand, oak logs, netherrack, cactus, chorus fruit or sea pickles give five results. Sand, red and plain sandstone, cobblestone, cobbled deepslate, clay, clay balls and wet sponge stay one-to-one, because crushing, milling, quenching, leaching, tumbling, mixing or brick washing could reverse them and multiply items.
guide.arcana_industry.smoke_rack.page5: The rack also dries rotten flesh into leather, soul sand into soul soil, and mossy cobblestone into cobblestone. Hoppers or item pipes feed the top stock slot. Every 40 ticks a formed, lit rack processes four complete recipe batches; partial stock waits. The south face defaults to input: sneak-use it once with an empty hand to set output, then extract there with a pipe. Empty-hand use collects buffered output. Sneak-use any face to cycle input, output and disabled. The stock and output survive saves and chunk reloads; breaking the rack pauses processing. It has no FE or fluid port.
guide.arcana_industry.smoke_rack.page6: Smoke four white wool blocks on the lit rack into four Creosote Lagging. Smoke from the campfire impregnates the fibre with tar to make a flexible thermal wrap for the coil winding. The treated lagging goes in the bottom-center of the Induction Coiler controller craft; raw wool or old plank slats do not substitute. White wool is available from sheep before this Tier 4 gate.
guide.arcana_industry.blast_column.page1: Shape four clay balls around iron bars into a Green Tuyere, then fire it in the fuel-fired Kiln at 600 degrees for 180 ticks. The Ceramic Tuyere survives the furnace blast; the green body or loose bricks cannot replace it in the Blast Column controller craft. Craft the controller from four sealed steel plates, two magma blocks, two bricks, a blast furnace and this fired tuyere. Its tuyere channels the bosh air; the structure's four iron-bar sides represent the external air inlets. The Kiln is available before the Blast Column. It is a 3x3 blast furnace stack six courses tall (43 blocks plus the controller). Build it from the bottom up. Course 1, the hearth, is a blast furnace two blocks below the controller, ringed by eight stone bricks. Course 2, the bosh, is a magma block on top of the furnace with an iron-bar air inlet on each of its four sides and stone bricks in the corners. Course 3 holds the controller with a brick pillar in each corner; its four sides stay open so you can reach the controller. Course 4, the shaft, is a full ring of eight bricks around a source lava block placed directly above the controller; the ring keeps the lava from spreading. Course 5, the heat-recovery throat, has four brick sides and four copper-block corner sinks, leaving the center open. Course 6, the exhaust cap, has four iron-bar side vents; its center and corners remain open. The copper sinks sit above the shaft corners and the vents sit above the throat bricks. A Structure Projector bound to the controller shows each course in turn. Every block must stay in place. A stone brick in place of a brick stops the column.
guide.arcana_industry.blast_column.page2: Right-click the formed controller with four matching items to run one column_blasting batch. Four amethyst shards vitrify into one amethyst insert for the Resonance Infuser. Sand, cobblestone, clay balls and netherrack also produce useful construction materials. Removing any hearth, tuyere, pillar, shaft, copper sink or exhaust vent, the magma, the furnace or the source lava stops processing without consuming items.
guide.arcana_industry.blast_column.page3: Stone-variant batches smooth and polish quarried blocks at scale: stone, sandstone, red sandstone, quartz block and basalt each fire into their smooth form, while andesite, diorite, granite and blackstone polish directly. Cobbled deepslate fires into deepslate and red sand vitrifies into glass alongside ordinary sand. The shared heat returns five blocks per batch of four for netherrack, smooth stone, smooth quartz, smooth basalt, the four polished stones and red-sand glass. Sand, cobblestone, clay, sandstone, red sandstone and cobbled deepslate stay four for four because crushers, mills or quench vats turn their products back.
guide.arcana_industry.blast_column.page4: Specialty batches recover materials the furnace cannot: a full clay block fires into terracotta (distinct from the clay-ball-to-brick batch), wet sponges dry out, soul sand compacts into soul soil, and eight gravel fracture under heat into two flint shards.
guide.arcana_industry.blast_column.page5: The column uses arcana_industry:column_blasting datapack recipes exclusively; ordinary minecraft:blasting recipes do not run here. For manual use, the structure consumes only the held batch and drops output if the inventory is full. For automation, insert stock through the top or horizontal controller faces with a hopper or item pipe. The formed column runs one batch every 40 ticks and buffers products for extraction from the bottom. Sneak-use an empty hand on a face to cycle input, output and disabled; use an empty hand normally to collect buffered products. The stock and output buffers persist across saves. The column has no FE port.
Electrolyze purified salts into a conductive crystal. Cut four amethyst shards in a formed Resonance Basin to obtain a harmonic lens; vitrify one more four-shard batch in the formed Blast Column. Wind conductive crystals (three each) in a formed Induction Coiler into four Wound Coils: keep one for the infuser and realign the other three in a formed Magnetizer for a Magnetized Core. Charge four Compacted Electrodes in a formed Capacitor Array for a Charged Capacitor. Feed a worn redstone mechanism (piston, hopper, dropper, trapdoor and more), into a formed Arc Press for scrap ingots, or arc-weld two Sealed Steel Plates in it for a Fused Steel Plate. Craft the infuser with the Wound Coil, the Magnetized Core, the Fused Steel Plate, the crystal, one vitrified amethyst insert, the lens and a Resonant Rune, an electrolyzer and the Charged Capacitor. The rune is made by offering two conductive crystals and 200 lumen to an Astral Font; the separate conductive crystal slot remains mandatory. All six hand-fed structures and the Electrolyzer now gate this t4 apparatus; no plain ingredient remains in the craft.

Place a normal amethyst block directly against any side of the infuser. It is a permanent resonator, not a consumed ingredient. Without it, work pauses before taking FE. Feed the left slot and supply 16 FE/t for 120 ticks. Quartz becomes attuned quartz for the next stage.

Twenty datapack resonating recipes convert resources into useful lighting, redstone, dyes, building and end materials. JEI shows exact input counts, results, FE and the amethyst resonator condition. Recipe type: arcana_industry:resonating; fields ingredient, count, result, duration, energy_per_tick and optional priority.

Trait rule: the product may carry only the traits of count x input plus the resonator field (resonant 2, luminous 1). So quartz gains its faint glow as attuned quartz, five shards grow an amethyst cluster and twelve sculk condense an echo shard, but amethyst cannot become glowstone. A datapack row that breaks the rule pauses with the state Product traits not in input or field.

Top and horizontal faces import items; bottom exports. Configure each face in the GUI. FE enters from any side, or use the manual crank. Inventory, energy, progress and port modes persist across saves. Breaking the block drops stored items.

Resonating one sea lantern yields five prismarine crystals. Rebuilding a lantern in the Compaction Spire, Heliostat Etcher or Astral Relay uses at least five crystals per lantern. Six copper ingots resonate into two lightning rods; salvaging them returns at most three ingots each.
guide.arcana_industry.compaction_spire.p: Craft the controller with sealed steel plate, copper and iron blocks, and obsidian. Place obsidian below it and a redstone block above it. Put copper blocks directly east and west of it and two blocks out to the north and south (leaving the north and south faces open), and iron blocks at all four upper diagonal corners. One level higher, place pistons on the four horizontal sides around the empty center; cap the center one more level up with an iron block. The piston crown and cap complete the vertical compression frame. Use the Structure Projector to build it layer by layer.

Right-click the formed controller with enough material for two batches of its own loaded arcana_industry:compaction recipe. The spire loads exactly twice that recipe's input count into its stock buffer and refuses new feed while a batch is buffered or output is waiting. After the 40-tick cycle, use an empty hand to collect both outputs. It stops if any frame block, crown piston, compression cap, or base is missing.

Automation: hoppers or pipes feed the open north face (any face defaults to input), which buffers stock. Every 40 ticks the formed spire consumes two batches of the loaded recipe at once and stores both outputs in its product buffer; a single batch waits until the second arrives. Sneak-use the south face with an empty hand to switch it to output and pull products with a hopper or pipe; the bottom face is output by default but is covered by obsidian. An empty hand collects the buffer, and a broken frame pauses processing without losing stock.

Compaction recipes are distinct from the Press's pressing recipes: four redstone compact into one compacted electrode, two gravel into flint, one clay ball into a brick, nine bone meal into a bone block and four snowballs into packed ice. One electrode is required in the t2 Leaching Vat craft and two more in the Electrolyzer craft alongside purified salts. It needs no FE. JEI lists its compaction recipes under the Compaction Spire catalyst, with the doubled input and two separate output stacks shown.

Fifteen more batches round the Spire out to twenty: sand into sandstone, red sand into red sandstone, quartz into quartz block, prismarine shards into prismarine and prismarine crystals into sea lantern, magma cream into magma block and nine packed ice into one blue ice, nine slime balls into a slime block, glowstone dust into glowstone, nine nether wart into a nether wart block, honeycomb into honeycomb block, three rabbit hides into one leather (one fewer than the crafting grid needs), nine gold or iron nuggets back into an ingot, and nine dried kelp into a dried kelp block. Packed ice chains from the snowball batch above it into blue ice at the vanilla crafting ratio; the Spire takes eighteen packed ice for its doubled batch.
Prismarine crystals compact five to one sea lantern (ten crystals for the spire's doubled batch). Rinsing, resonating and scoring recover no more than five crystals per lantern.
guide.arcana_industry.compression_packin: Braid four string around a charcoal core to make two Compression Packing rings. Card two plant inputs in the Fiber Carder, then craft two Carded Fiber into four string; charcoal comes from smelted logs. The dark ring is a simplified shaft gland seal, distinct from the bronze bushing that supports the shaft.

A Monel Pump Blank uses four nickel ingots, two copper ingots, one Sintered Bronze Bushing, one Compression Packing gland and one Rotary Lip Seal. Make the lip seal from a second Compression Packing, leather contact lip, iron-nugget garter spring and Bearing Grease; mix honeycomb wax with clay for two grease before the Prism Separator is available; later, Rendered Tallow from porkchop separation can replace the wax. Packing seals the stationary gland while the spring-loaded lip excludes splashes at the rotating shaft. Two blanks result; the Copper Hot Press turns each into a Bath Circulation Pump in 240 ticks at 14 FE/t. Feed its item input from above or sides and extract below. The Silvering Bath requires this pump; loose packing cannot replace the finished lip seal. JEI lists both crafts and the press route.
guide.arcana_industry.basalt_temperer.pa: Build this t1 Thermal furnace from a Kiln, pistons, a furnace, blackstone and redstone. Feed FE to temper stone and mineral stock.
Temper one blackstone into Tempered Blackstone. Put it in the top-center slot of the Soaking Hearth controller craft; plain blackstone no longer works there.

Twenty datapack recipes of type arcana_industry:stone_tempering heat-treat stone, clay, ore, food and nether stock. Raw ore, stone, basalt, quartz, netherrack, red sand, kelp and chorus run in batches of 4 for 5. Each defines ingredient, count, result, duration, energy_per_tick and optional priority; JEI shows the loaded recipes.
Insert stock from top or sides, collect output below, and supply FE. Configure face modes in the menu; inventory, FE, progress and ports persist through reloads.
guide.arcana_industry.soaking_hearth.pag: Craft the controller from cured hearth brick, Tempered Blackstone from the Basalt Temperer, nether bricks, plain blackstone and a furnace. Place a blackstone block directly beneath it and iron bars directly above it. Wall all four horizontal sides with nether bricks.

Right-click the formed controller while holding one full soaking recipe batch. It loads the stock buffer; after 40 ticks, right-click with an empty hand to collect the product. A short batch or full stock buffer leaves your held items intact. A missing blackstone base, iron bars cap, or any open nether brick wall stops operation.

It runs 20 exclusive datapack soaking recipes; JEI shows each batch size. Four iron, gold or copper ingots soak into one Soaked Billet. Four raw iron or raw copper roast into three grit; four raw gold or one gold block yield gilded blackstone (1 or 2). An iron block draws seven chains, and a copper block weathers to exposed copper. Blaze powder (2) or a blaze rod makes three fire charges, four magma cream render two slime balls, four nether brick fire into cracked nether bricks and four quartz into smooth quartz. Four amethyst shards fuse into tinted glass, six glowstone dust into shroomlight, four redstone into glowstone dust and four lapis into blue glazed terracotta. Two diamonds seed a budding amethyst, and four netherite scrap press a netherite upgrade template. Every route is lossy; hold the batch and right-click, or automate as below.

Soak an iron ingot into a Soaked Billet to replace one of the Quench Vat's four iron ingot corners. This makes the Soaking Hearth the third required t1 apparatus alongside the Kiln and Quench Vat; a bare iron ingot in that corner no longer satisfies the vat's craft.

For automation, insert valid soaking stock into the controller from any face except the bottom and extract products from the bottom; reach these covered faces through Stock Hatches. Each formed batch takes 40 ticks; a missing blackstone base, iron bars cap or nether brick wall pauses processing without consuming stock. The controller buffers one input stack and one output stack, saves both and its face modes, and exposes Forge item handlers to hoppers or pipes; stock with no matching recipe is refused. Sneak-right-click with an empty hand to cycle the clicked face through input, output and disabled; right-click with an empty hand to collect buffered output. It has no FE or fluid port. Matching ties resolve by resource ID.

Stock Hatches: every face of this controller is covered by a frame part, so hoppers and pipes reach it through Stock Hatches. Place a hatch instead of any part that touches the controller face-to-face; at most two hatches may stand in, and a third breaks formation. A hatch relays only while the frame is formed, and it relays the controller face it covers: insert stock into a hatch on an In face, and extract products from a hatch whose face you sneak-use with an empty hand to cycle to Out (the base face starts as Out). For example, swap one side part for a hatch fed by a hopper pointing into it from beside, and swap the base part for a hatch with a hopper beneath it. A hopper touching a redstone block or other powered part is locked by vanilla rules. Right-clicking a hatch with an empty hand collects the product buffer.
guide.arcana_industry.char_retort.page1: Craft the Char Retort from four iron ingots, two brick blocks, copper, a hopper and a Kiln. Rows: iron/copper/iron; bricks/Kiln/bricks; iron/hopper/iron. Char one bricks block into a Carbon Brick; it replaces the upper-left plain bricks block in the Ember Dryer craft.
guide.arcana_industry.char_retort.page2: The retort runs 21 charring recipes. Any log or stem (the minecraft:logs tag) gives two charcoal, and a bamboo block gives one. The other recipes are: two bones to black dye (bone black); cocoa to brown dye; kelp to dried kelp; podzol to coarse dirt; grass to dirt; mud to packed mud; nylium to netherrack; saplings to dead bushes; glow ink to ink; two gravel to flint; mossy stone bricks back to stone bricks; heat-cracked stone, nether, deepslate brick/tile and blackstone bricks; quartz block to smooth quartz; and bricks to the Carbon Brick gate material. Cocoa, kelp, deepslate bricks and quartz blocks are bulk jobs: four in, five out, better than a furnace. Each tick uses 8 FE, and a recipe takes 40-160 ticks. Feed FE through Forge energy or use the menu crank. A 22nd recipe chars two Carbon Face Blanks into two Carbon Seal Faces (160 ticks, 12 FE/t) for the Mechanical Face Seal; see the Phase Fermenter entry.
guide.arcana_industry.char_retort.page3: Top and horizontal faces import items; the bottom exports. Set any face Off, In or Out from the menu. Hoppers and Forge item handlers can automate input and output. The two slots, energy, progress and side settings persist on save/load; work pauses when the output is full.
guide.arcana_industry.char_retort.page4: Datapacks add charring recipes under data/<namespace>/recipes with type arcana_industry:charring, ingredient (item or tag), count, result, duration, energy_per_tick and optional priority. Higher priority wins, then ascending recipe ID. JEI shows inputs, outputs, time, FE and the Char Retort catalyst; JEI is optional.
guide.arcana_industry.clay_extruder.page: Craft the fifth t0 machine from iron ingots, Crusher-made copper grit, two pistons and a hopper. No Kiln output is needed.

Load one clay block to form one firebrick. This is the only source of Formed Firebrick; it replaces the upper-left plain brick in the Kiln craft. Stone and brick batches give 5 slabs per 2 blocks and 4 planks give 9 slabs, beating the stonecutter. Sandstone and cobbled deepslate stay at 2 slabs per block because reclamation would loop them.
Twenty datapack recipes use arcana_industry:extruding with ingredient, count, result, duration, energy_per_tick and optional priority. JEI lists the loaded recipes and the Extruder catalyst.
Supply FE, insert materials from top or sides, and extract below. Configure each face in the menu; inventory, FE, progress and ports save across reloads.
guide.arcana_industry.boiler_turbine.pag: The Boiler Turbine is the Low-class (64 V) generator, the step after the Firebox Dynamo. Craft it on a crafting table: iron ingot (forge:ingots/iron), Copper Cable, iron ingot on top; bucket, Firebox Dynamo, bucket in the middle; iron ingot, piston, iron ingot on the bottom. Mine it with a stone pickaxe or better; it drops its fuel and residue when broken.

Use: fill the 16,000 mB tank by right-clicking with a water bucket, and load fuel by right-clicking with it. Each steam_raising batch boils 3-16 mB of water per tick, and every mB gives 16 FE (48-256 FE/t). Examples: 8 coal boil 8 mB/t for 6,400 ticks (819,200 FE, 51,200 mB) and leave 2 Temper Ash. 2 blaze rods give 256 FE/t. A lava bucket returns its bucket. A jukebox gives back its diamond. Dense fuels give more FE per item than in the dynamo, but each batch needs water.

Condition: a tick only burns when the tank holds that tick's water and the 128,000 FE buffer has room. Otherwise the fire stays banked, and no fuel, water or energy is lost. A batch lights only when its residue fits the residue slot. Right-click with an empty hand to read the buffer, water, burn time and FE/t, and to take out the residue. Everything is saved with the world. Water cannot be drained back out, and nothing can charge the buffer.

Automation: pipes using the Forge fluid capability fill the tank from any face (water only). Hoppers insert fuel from any face, and extraction only removes residue. Each tick it pushes up to 256 FE into adjacent Low-class (Tier 2-3) or untagged machines. A Copper Cable touching it pulls from the buffer. Tin Wire and higher-class cables need a transformer; a wrong-class run is refused like any source. Recipes: data/<namespace>/recipes/steam_raising, type arcana_industry:steam_raising, with fields ingredient, count, residue, burn_time (1-72000), steam_per_tick (1-16) and priority (highest wins, then recipe ID). JEI shows a Steam Raising category with the turbine as its catalyst.
guide.arcana_industry.firebox_dynamo.pag: The Firebox Dynamo is this mod's own Forge Energy (FE) generator. Craft it on a crafting table: three iron ingots (forge:ingots/iron) on top, Tin Wire, a Furnace and Tin Wire in the middle, and copper ingot, redstone dust (forge:dusts/redstone), copper ingot on the bottom row. It is mined with a stone pickaxe or better and drops its fuel and residue when broken.

Use: load fuel by right-clicking the dynamo with it; only items with a combustion recipe are accepted. Each recipe burns a whole batch at once and sets the output: 4 coal give 6,400 ticks at 20 FE/t (128,000 FE) and leave 1 Temper Ash, a lava bucket gives 20,000 ticks at 20 FE/t and returns its empty bucket, a blaze rod runs hot at 32 FE/t and crumbles to blaze powder. Wood burns at 12-16 FE/t into charcoal or fine ash (light gray dye), wool into gray dye, saplings, bamboo and kelp blocks into bone meal. Metal and minerals survive the fire: crossbows, smithing tables and tripwire hooks leave iron nuggets, note blocks redstone, daylight detectors quartz.

Condition: a fuel is only lit when its first tick fits the 32,000 FE buffer and its residue fits the residue slot (same item, under a full stack), so no fuel or residue is ever lost; empty the residue to keep it running. The grate glows and the dynamo gives light while burning. Right-click with an empty hand to read the buffer, burn time and current FE/t and to take out residue. The buffer, burn, rate and both slots are saved with the world. The dynamo only gives energy: no cable, machine or other generator can charge it.

Automation: hoppers and item pipes insert fuel through any face into the fuel slot; extraction from any face (a hopper below) only removes residue, never unburnt fuel. Every tick the dynamo pushes up to 32 FE into adjacent Trickle-class (Tier 0-1) machines, and any cable touching it pulls from its buffer (see Power Cables). Its power is Trickle class (16 V): it feeds Tin Wire directly, and touching a higher-class cable gives nothing. To collect several dynamos into a 64 V Copper Cable line, run their Tin Wire into a Trickle-Low Transformer set to Step up.

Recipes are datapack JSON under data/<namespace>/recipes/combustion. Type: arcana_industry:combustion. Fields: ingredient (item or tag), count (default 1), residue (item/count, required), burn_time (1-72000 ticks), energy_per_tick (1-64), priority (default 0). Highest priority wins; equal priorities use ascending recipe ID. With Just Enough Items installed, the Combustion category lists every fuel with its FE/t, total FE and residue, and the dynamo is its catalyst. JEI is optional.
guide.arcana_industry.clinker_oven.page1: Craft the Clinker Oven from four iron ingots, two blackstone blocks, two pistons, a hopper and a Kiln. Rows: iron/blackstone/iron; piston/Kiln/piston; iron/hopper/iron. Clinker one bricks block into a Clinker Brick; it replaces the upper-right plain bricks block in the Ember Dryer craft. Material update: crafting slot 1 (row-major 3x3) now requires a tungsten ingot via forge:ingots/tungsten; all existing progression gates remain required.
guide.arcana_industry.clinker_oven.page2: The oven heat-shatters 19 stone and deepslate variants into Gravel for screening, and turns a bricks block into the Clinker Brick required for the Ember Dryer. It vitrifies the clay bond of a Green Grinding Wheel into the Vitrified Grinding Wheel that the Lens Grinder craft needs (240 ticks, 14 FE/t). It fires a Green Porcelain Insulator (shapeless: four clay balls, one Screened Silica and one diorite as the feldspar flux; makes two) into the white Porcelain Insulator the Arc Press craft needs (220 ticks, 13 FE/t); hoppers can feed green insulators in and pull fired ones out like any other clinkering job. It also cures a Filled Dry-Lube Bearing into the Cured Dry-Lube Bearing the Coal Forge craft needs (200 ticks, 12 FE/t). It also runs 16 distinct furnace-equivalent heat jobs: sand to glass, raw iron to an ingot, clay balls to bricks, netherrack to nether bricks, cactus or sea pickles to dyes, chorus fruit to popped fruit, potatoes to baked potatoes, kelp to dried kelp, and beef, pork, chicken, mutton, rabbit, cod and salmon to cooked food. Cooking, dye, chorus, kelp, netherrack and raw-iron jobs take four inputs for five outputs; glass, bricks and baked potatoes stay one-to-one. Each uses 120 ticks and 8 FE/t. Stone jobs use 10-28 FE/t; the Clinker Brick takes 120 ticks. It fires a Green Assay Crucible into the Clay-Graphite Assay Crucible the Assay Cupel Hearth craft needs (220 ticks, 14 FE/t); hoppers can feed and empty it. It also brazes a Prepared Braze Joint into a Brazed Joint (200 ticks, 12 FE/t), required for the Induction Coiler contact seam. Feed prepared joints through the input port and extract finished joints from the output port.
guide.arcana_industry.clinker_oven.page3: Top and horizontal faces import items; the bottom exports. Set any face Off, In or Out from the menu. Hoppers and Forge item handlers can automate input and output. The two slots, energy, progress and side settings persist on save/load; work pauses when the output is full.
guide.arcana_industry.clinker_oven.page4: Datapacks add clinkering recipes under data/<namespace>/recipes with type arcana_industry:clinkering, ingredient (item or tag), count, result, duration, energy_per_tick and optional priority. Higher priority wins, then ascending recipe ID. JEI shows inputs, outputs, time, FE and the Clinker Oven catalyst; JEI is optional.
guide.arcana_industry.clinker_oven.page5: For t6 thermal insulation, feed two magma blocks into the powered Clinker Oven. Its 220-tick, 14 FE/t mineral-fibre treatment yields one Mineral Fibre Lagging. Insert from top or an input side, supply FE, and extract the finished mat from bottom or an output side. JEI lists the clinkering recipe; use the lagging in the top middle of the Heat Exchanger craft.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_font.page1: Craft the Astral Font early from four quartz, two amethyst shards, glass, a copper ingot and an iron ingot. Place it beneath open sky before the first Kiln. At night it gathers five lumen every second, up to 1,000. It does not accept FE and industrial machinery cannot generate lumen.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_font.page2: Adjacent fonts exchange up to four lumen every five ticks, flowing from the fuller font to the emptier one. A covered font can therefore receive lumen from an outdoor font; loaded chunks are required.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_font.page3: Offering Ring: surround one Astral Font at its own height with four gold blocks on the north, south, east and west sides and four amethyst blocks on the diagonals. Power the font with redstone, for example a redstone block directly beneath it, and drop amethyst shards onto its top. Every four seconds the formed, powered ring consumes one shard for 160 lumen, even in daylight. It pauses if fewer than 160 lumen fit in the 1,000-lumen store; no offering is wasted. A downward-facing dropper above the font can feed shards automatically, and adjacent fonts above or below can carry the result onward. The ring never accepts FE or industrial energy. Break one frame block or remove redstone power to stop it; loose offerings can still despawn normally.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_font.page4: Pedestal rites use the same powered gold-amethyst ring as shard offerings. Place one item on top of each of the four diagonal amethyst blocks, then drop the center ingredient on the font. Every four seconds, if at least the listed lumen is stored, the font consumes exactly one item at each position and drops the result above itself. The ring must stay formed and redstone-powered. Two starting recipes: an echo shard plus four sculk and 300 lumen make a sculk sensor; a prismarine crystal plus four prismarine shards and 220 lumen make a sea lantern. Neither rite adds traits absent from its inputs. Droppers aimed at each pedestal and the center can feed it; collect the output with a hopper minecart or other item collector. Data packs can add arcana_industry:pedestal_rite recipes with center, corner, lumen_cost and result fields. Matching recipes resolve by alphabetically first ID. Keep the center clear when feeding to prevent stray items blocking a rite.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_font.page5: Sacrificial pedestal rite: with the powered ring formed, put one echo shard on the Font and one sculk vein on each diagonal pedestal. Bring a living zombie within one block of the Font at item height. At the next four-second check, 360 lumen, one of each item, and the zombie are consumed to make a sculk catalyst. The zombie is removed without ordinary loot or experience. A missing zombie or insufficient lumen leaves all offerings and the mob intact. Keep the ritual contained: a powered ring will consume any matching zombie in its center, including one led there by another player. JEI lists the required mob. Data packs may set an optional sacrifice entity ID on pedestal_rite recipes; missing IDs mean no mob is needed. An item collector can take the catalyst.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_font.page6: Use an empty hand on a font holding at least 100 lumen to gain 30 seconds of night vision. The action spends 100 lumen. Breaking a font drops the block, while stored lumen is lost; place it before nightfall. A font with 100+ lumen on a Concordance Altar diagonal corner adds 2 altar stability and pays 100 lumen per fusion that needs it.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_font.page7: Hold an item the font recognizes and use it on the font to perform a lumen rite: the font consumes the held item and lumen, then gives you the result (dropping it if your inventory is full). A font too low on lumen refuses the rite and keeps the item. Data packs add rites with the arcana_industry:lumen_rite recipe type. A successful rite sounds a rising three-note glass tone; silence with the same held item means no rite fired.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_font.page8: Known rites: 8 feathers + 150 lumen yield 1 phantom membrane; 8 sculk + 220 lumen yield 1 echo shard; 4 rotten flesh + 60 lumen yield 1 leather; 1 glow ink sac + 40 lumen yields 2 glowstone dust; 6 glow berries + 50 lumen yield 1 glowstone dust. A rite only concentrates what its offering already holds (see Material Traits), so it never turns one metal into another. When several rites accept the held stack, the rite with the alphabetically first recipe ID is performed. Rites can also run unattended in a rite basin (see the last page).
guide.arcana_industry.astral_font.page9: More rites: 5 string + 60 lumen yield 1 cobweb; 6 honeycomb + 60 lumen yield 2 honey bottles; 6 gunpowder + 80 lumen yield 3 fire charges; 4 spider eyes + 90 lumen yield 2 fermented spider eyes; 5 leather + 120 lumen yield 1 saddle; 8 prismarine shards + 120 lumen yield 4 prismarine crystals; 8 feathers + 150 lumen yield 1 phantom membrane.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_font.page10: Concentration rites: 4 magma cream + 140 lumen yield 2 blaze powder; 5 turtle scutes + 160 lumen yield 1 nautilus shell; 6 prismarine crystals + 180 lumen yield 1 sea lantern; 6 rabbit hide + 180 lumen yield 1 rabbit's foot; 3 blaze powder + 200 lumen yield 1 blaze rod; 2 echo shards + 240 lumen yield 1 sculk sensor; 8 popped chorus fruit + 260 lumen yield 1 shulker shell; 2 amethyst blocks (crafted from 8 shards) + 400 lumen yield 1 budding amethyst; 8 nautilus shells + 480 lumen yield 1 heart of the sea. Lumen powers a rite but adds no property: the product may only hold material traits that the offered stack carries (see Material Traits). The font refuses any rite, including a data-pack rite of the arcana_industry:lumen_rite type, whose product would invent a trait, and spends nothing.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_font.page11: Early progression rite: use one amethyst shard on a font holding at least 40 lumen to form a Night Sigil. The Kiln craft consumes one sigil; wait for night, keep the font sky-exposed, and perform the rite before attempting the thermal workshop. No industrial recipe creates the sigil.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_font.page12: Pressing-tier rite: once the Kiln fires Annealed Copper, use two of them on a font holding at least 80 lumen to form a Temper Glyph. The Pressure Press craft consumes one glyph in its top-right slot. Automation can stock the copper, but the rite itself is performed at the font and no industrial recipe creates the glyph.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_font.page13: Aqueous-tier rite: once the Pressure Press makes Sealed Steel Plates, use one on a font holding at least 120 lumen to form a Brine Ward. The Leaching Vat craft consumes one ward in its bottom-center slot. Automation can stock the plates, but the rite is performed at the font and no industrial recipe creates the ward.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_font.page14: Electrical-tier rite: once the Leaching Vat yields Purified Salts, offer two to a font holding at least 160 lumen to form an Ion Seal. The Electrolyzer craft consumes one seal in its bottom-left slot. Salts can be piped in by automation, but the seal only comes from the font rite; no machine recipe makes it.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_font.page15: Resonant-tier rite: after the Electrolyzer makes Conductive Crystals, offer two to a font holding at least 200 lumen to form a Resonant Rune. The Resonance Infuser craft consumes one rune in its middle-right slot as well as a separate conductive crystal. This rite must be performed at the font; machines cannot create the rune.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_font.page16: Solar-tier rite: once the Resonance Infuser attunes quartz, offer two Attuned Quartz to a font holding at least 240 lumen to form a Dawn Emblem. The Heliostat Etcher craft consumes one emblem in its bottom-left slot in addition to its own attuned quartz slot. Perform it at night or bank lumen through adjacent fonts; machines cannot create the emblem.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_font.page17: Prismatic-tier rite: after the Heliostat Etcher makes Solar Prisms, offer two to a font with at least 280 lumen to make a Prism Mandala. The Prism Separator craft consumes one mandala in its bottom-left slot and a separate Solar Prism. The rite is performed at the font; automation can stock the prisms but cannot create the mandala.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_font.page18: Lattice-tier rite: after the Prism Separator yields Prism Cores, offer two to a font with at least 320 lumen to make a Core Halo. The Lattice Composer craft consumes one halo in its bottom-left slot and a separate Prism Core. The rite is performed at the font; automation can stock the cores but cannot create the halo.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_font.page19: Phase-tier rite: after the Lattice Composer makes Phase Lattice, offer two to a font with at least 360 lumen to make a Phase Sigil. The Phase Annealer craft consumes one sigil in its bottom-right slot and a separate phase lattice. A single night yields up to 1,000 lumen, so bank the cost through adjacent fonts if needed. Machines cannot create the sigil.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_font.page20: Capstone rite: after the Phase Conflux yields Converged Phase, offer two to a font with at least 480 lumen to make a Phase Heart. The Phase Scepter craft consumes one heart in its top-center slot. Converged Phase needs the whole Modulator, Stabilizer, Preserver, Effuser and Conflux line, so the heart is the last font rite of the t9 phase tier; no machine creates it.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_font.page21: Rite basin automation: without the gold-amethyst ring, power a font with redstone (a lever or redstone block beside it) and place a hopper, chest or other item container directly beneath it. Every four seconds the font checks the items resting on its top, adds up identical dropped stacks, and performs one hand-rite recipe from the list above, including the tier rites. The rite spends the same lumen and offerings and inserts the result into the container below. It waits without consuming anything if lumen is short, power is off, nothing is below, or the full result does not fit. A downward dropper above the font can feed offerings. The font itself still has no item or FE interface, and only night sky or ring offerings refill its lumen.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page1: Craft with an amethyst shard, a blaze rod and a gold ingot, in that column. The wand holds no lumen itself; it draws charge only from a nearby Astral Font.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page2: Right-click to cast the wand's current spell. It searches a six block radius around you for the fullest Astral Font holding enough lumen, spends the cost from it, then fires. If no font nearby holds enough lumen, nothing is spent and you are told so.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page3: Lumen Bolt costs 40 lumen and strikes the first living target along a straight line up to 12 blocks, dealing 6 magic damage. Resonance Pulse costs 65 lumen and damages nearby hostile creatures within 4 blocks for 3 magic damage, slowing them briefly; passive creatures are spared.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page4: Astral Lance costs 90 lumen and pierces every living creature along its line up to 16 blocks, dealing 4 magic damage to each and making them glow briefly, unlike Lumen Bolt which stops at the first target.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page5: Starfall costs 110 lumen and lands its damage at the point you are aiming at, up to 20 blocks away, rather than along a line. Every living creature within 3 blocks of that impact point takes 7 magic damage and catches fire for 3 seconds, striking a cluster of enemies at range instead of whatever stands directly between you and them.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page6: Arc Chain costs 55 lumen and strikes the first living target along a line up to 14 blocks for 5 magic damage, then leaps to the nearest other living creature within 5 blocks of the one it just struck, dealing 3 magic damage and weakening each creature it touches. It makes up to two leaps in total, each needing another target close enough, spreading damage across a scattered group instead of hitting one spot or one line.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page7: Dusk Fan costs 75 lumen and strikes hostile creatures within 6 blocks in a forward cone. Each takes 4 magic damage and is blinded for 4 seconds. Creatures behind you and passive animals are spared, making it useful when facing a group near allies or livestock.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page8: Gravity Well costs 85 lumen and forms a pull point where you aim, up to 16 blocks away. Hostile creatures within 4 blocks take 2 magic damage, are pulled toward the point, and are slowed for 3 seconds. Passive animals are spared. Use it to gather scattered enemies before another attack.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page9: Repulsion Burst costs 70 lumen and deals 3 magic damage to hostile creatures within 4 blocks, pushing them away from you. Passive animals and distant enemies are spared. Use it to create room when surrounded; keep an Astral Font nearby to supply the wand.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page10: Skyward Surge costs 80 lumen and deals 3 magic damage to hostile creatures within 4 blocks, launching them upward. Passive animals and distant enemies are spared. Use it to interrupt nearby attackers or gain room to escape; the wand still needs a charged Astral Font within reach.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page11: Withering Sigil costs 95 lumen and strikes the nearest hostile creature within 8 blocks for 2 magic damage, then inflicts Wither for 5 seconds. Other hostile creatures and passive animals are spared. Use it against a tough single enemy; the wand draws its charge from a nearby Astral Font.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page12: Siphon Mark costs 100 lumen and strikes the nearest hostile creature within 6 blocks for 3 magic damage. When the strike lands, it restores 2 health to you, up to your normal maximum. It spares passive creatures and other hostiles; a blocked strike gives no healing.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page13: Nullifying Brand costs 105 lumen and strikes the nearest hostile creature within 8 blocks for 4 magic damage. A successful strike strips that creature's beneficial status effects, such as Resistance or Strength, while leaving harmful effects in place. Other hostiles and passive creatures are spared; a blocked strike does not dispel effects.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page14: Binding Snare costs 60 lumen and deals 2 magic damage to every hostile creature within 5 blocks. It also roots them in place for 3 seconds, halting their movement outright, and clears any motion they already had. Passive creatures are untouched. Use it to stop a group from closing in or to hold enemies still for a follow-up spell.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page15: Finishing Gleam costs 90 lumen and strikes the nearest hostile within 8 blocks. It deals 2 magic damage to an unwounded target, plus 1 damage for every 2 health that target is missing, capped at 10 damage. Other hostiles and passive creatures are spared. Wound a durable enemy first, then use this spell to finish it efficiently.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page16: Aegis Ward costs 120 lumen and is mainly defensive. As it forms, the ward flares outward and deals 2 magic damage to every hostile within 3 blocks, sparing passive animals and anything farther away. Casting it also grants 10 seconds of Absorption and a reflecting ward. Any living creature that lands a hit on you while the ward holds takes 3 magic damage bounced straight back at it, so an attacker that keeps swinging keeps paying for it. Use it before wading into a melee you expect to take hits in.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page17: Harmonic Reversal costs 115 lumen and sends a pulse 5 blocks around you. Every hostile creature in range takes 3 magic damage, while you and each nearby living non-hostile recover up to 2 health, limited by their normal maximum. It still heals if no hostile is nearby. Use it to protect livestock and companions while pushing back attackers; distant creatures are untouched.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page18: Blink Strike costs 130 lumen and, unlike every other spell, moves you instead of just striking: you blink up to 6 blocks forward along the direction you are facing, stopping short of any solid wall in the way rather than passing through it. On arrival, every hostile within 3 blocks of where you land takes 4 magic damage. Use it to close distance on a fleeing target or to jump into the middle of a scattered group.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page19: Discordant Call costs 95 lumen. It finds the nearest pair of hostile mobs within 8 blocks of you and 5 blocks of each other, deals 2 magic damage to each, then turns them against one another. It leaves passive creatures and unpaired hostiles alone. Cast near a cluster to redirect attackers while you retreat; the spell still consumes lumen if no eligible pair is present.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page20: Rift Exchange costs 110 lumen. It swaps the positions of the two nearest hostile mobs within 8 blocks of you and deals 3 magic damage to each. Use it to pull a distant attacker into another's position or disrupt two approaching enemies. Passive creatures and hostiles outside the radius are untouched; lumen is still spent if fewer than two hostiles qualify.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page21: Arcane Fury costs 100 lumen. It strikes the nearest hostile within 4 blocks for 4 magic damage as you enter the fight, then grants 10 seconds of Strength II and Speed II. It spares passive creatures and distant hostiles; you still gain the buffs when no hostile is nearby. Cast it before closing into melee or pursuing a fleeing target.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page22: Shift-right-click cycles the wand's spell mode through Lumen Bolt, Resonance Pulse, Astral Lance, Starfall, Arc Chain, Dusk Fan, Gravity Well, Repulsion Burst, Skyward Surge, Withering Sigil, Siphon Mark, Nullifying Brand, Binding Snare, Finishing Gleam, Aegis Ward, Harmonic Reversal, Blink Strike, Discordant Call, Rift Exchange and Arcane Fury in order. The selected mode is stored on the wand, so you can prepare it before approaching a Font.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page23: Casting has a short cooldown between uses. Industrial power cannot substitute for lumen; only Astral Fonts under open night sky supply this offense.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page24: Every spell has its own impact sound, played where it actually lands rather than at you: a bolt cracks, a pulse thumps, a curse sours, a ward rings. A miss stays silent, so the sound tells you which creatures were struck even out of sight. At most four impacts sound per cast, and an Aegis Ward reflection rings with the ward's impact.
guide.arcana_industry.chromium_ore.page1: Chromium Ore and Deepslate Chromium Ore generate in the Overworld between Y -48 and 32 (veins of size 5, up to four veins per chunk column). An iron pickaxe or better is required. Silk Touch keeps the block; ordinary mining drops Raw Chromium and Fortune can increase the yield. Required industrial use: quench vat. Its craft consumes this ingot; compatible forge:ingots/chromium inputs are accepted.
guide.arcana_industry.chromium_ore.page2: Raw Chromium is chromite: a furnace or blast furnace cannot reduce it. The Crusher turns one Raw Chromium into two Chromium Grit in 180 ticks at 5 energy per tick. Craft two Chromium Grit with one Aluminum Grit into two Chromium Thermite Charges (the aluminum is the reductant). Fire each charge in the Fuel-fired Kiln at full 1000 heat for 120 ticks for one Chromium Ingot; a Solar Furnace can also ignite the charge. Automate by piping Crusher output into a crafter or stockpile, then feed charges into the Kiln top face with fuel on the sides and extract ingots below.
guide.arcana_industry.chromium_ore.page3: Chromium uses forge:ores/chromium, forge:raw_materials/chromium and forge:ingots/chromium tags. Datapacks can add matching recipes. Chromium Ingots are stored for later apparatus and material progression. A Lattice Composer combines 2 tagged chromium ingots with one furnace to make a smoker for fast food processing. Feed both slots from the upper or side item ports, provide 24 FE/t for 160 ticks, and extract below. The binder is consumed.
guide.arcana_industry.cobalt_ore.page1: Cobalt Ore and Deepslate Cobalt Ore generate in the Overworld between Y -64 and -16, a deep and scarce band (veins of size 4, up to two veins per chunk column). A diamond pickaxe or better is required. Silk Touch keeps the block; ordinary mining drops Raw Cobalt and Fortune can increase the yield. Required industrial use: polarity inverter. Its craft consumes this ingot; compatible forge:ingots/cobalt inputs are accepted.
guide.arcana_industry.cobalt_ore.page2: Smelt or blast Raw Cobalt into Cobalt Ingots. The Crusher processes one Raw Cobalt into two Cobalt Grit, each of which can be smelted or blasted into an ingot. Feed the Crusher through an input face and extract its output with a hopper or item capability; furnace or blast furnace automation handles the grit.
guide.arcana_industry.cobalt_ore.page3: Cobalt uses forge:ores/cobalt, forge:raw_materials/cobalt and forge:ingots/cobalt tags. Datapacks can add matching recipes. Cobalt Ingots are stored for later apparatus and material progression. A Lattice Welder joins 2 tagged cobalt ingots into a pair of hard-edged shears in 160 ticks at 22 FE/t; feed the top or side ports and extract below.
guide.arcana_industry.gallium_ore.page1: Gallium Ore and Deepslate Gallium Ore generate deep in the Overworld between Y -64 and 40 (veins of size 6, at most one vein per chunk column). An iron pickaxe or better is required. Silk Touch keeps the block; ordinary mining drops Raw Gallium and Fortune can increase the yield. Required industrial use: diffraction grate. Its craft consumes this ingot; compatible forge:ingots/gallium inputs are accepted.
guide.arcana_industry.gallium_ore.page2: Smelt or blast Raw Gallium into Gallium Ingots. The Crusher processes one Raw Gallium into two Gallium Grit in 200 ticks at 6 energy per tick; each grit smelts or blasts into an ingot. Feed the Crusher through an input face and extract its output with a hopper or item capability, then automate a furnace or blast furnace.
guide.arcana_industry.gallium_ore.page3: Gallium uses forge:ores/gallium, forge:raw_materials/gallium and forge:ingots/gallium tags. Datapacks can add matching recipes. Gallium sits between Hafnium and Indium in generation height, so the two-grit Crusher route is a worthwhile trade of 1,200 energy per raw ore when fortune is unavailable. The powered Lattice Laminator also presses 2 forge:ingots/gallium into a daylight detector in 160 ticks at 24 FE/t; detector recyclers return only oak planks, never gallium.
guide.arcana_industry.germanium_ore.page: Germanium Ore and Deepslate Germanium Ore generate deep in the Overworld between Y -64 and 16 (veins of size 6, at most one vein per chunk column). An iron pickaxe or better is required. Silk Touch keeps the block; ordinary mining drops Raw Germanium and Fortune can increase the yield. Required industrial use: lattice infuser. Its craft consumes this ingot; compatible forge:ingots/germanium inputs are accepted.

Smelt or blast Raw Germanium into Germanium Ingots. The Crusher processes one Raw Germanium into two Germanium Grit in 200 ticks at 6 energy per tick; each grit smelts or blasts into an ingot. Feed the Crusher through an input face and extract its output with a hopper or item capability, then automate a furnace or blast furnace.

Germanium uses forge:ores/germanium, forge:raw_materials/germanium and forge:ingots/germanium tags. Datapacks can add matching recipes. Germanium completes the thirtieth and final modded ore family; the two-grit Crusher route yields two ingots per raw ore for 1,200 energy when Fortune is unavailable. The powered Lattice Laminator also laminates 2 forge:ingots/germanium into a spyglass in 160 ticks at 24 FE/t; spyglass recyclers return only a copper ingot, never germanium.
guide.arcana_industry.foundry_ring.page1: Craft the controller from sealed steel plates, furnaces and one Screened Silica from the Rotary Screen. Build a three-course foundry: a source lava hearth directly beneath the controller, four stone-brick sides and four iron-block corners below; three furnaces against the north, east and west faces, with the fourth furnace two blocks south so the controller's south face stays open; brick corners on its course. Above, place four iron-bar vents, two copper heat sinks at the north corners and two empty cauldrons as slag cups at the south corners. The top center stays open. North is fixed, so turn the whole arrangement to match the projector, not the controller (25 parts).
guide.arcana_industry.foundry_ring.page3: Its 21 exclusive foundry recipes cover three families: stone heating (tuff, andesite, blackstone, diorite, granite, prismarine, stone bricks, deepslate bricks, nether bricks, polished blackstone bricks, cobblestone to stone, clay ball to brick) and crude ore smelting (raw iron, raw gold, raw copper, diamond ore, lapis ore, redstone ore, nether gold ore, nether quartz ore). Fire eight brick blocks into eight Fired Foundry Liners; one liner is required for the Leaching Vat craft and another for the Electrolyzer craft, so the ring is a required t2 device. These recipes are separate from vanilla minecraft:smelting; a plain furnace will not process them and the ring will not accept other mods' furnace recipes. JEI lists all 21 under the Foundry Ring catalyst, showing the eightfold batch input and eight separate outputs. For automation, feed the open top from a hopper or pipe; the ring waits for eight matching batches, then runs them together. Sneak-right-click the exposed south controller face with an empty hand once to set it to output, and extract there with a pipe. Other faces may be set to input, output or disabled the same way. Stock pauses while the frame is broken and remains buffered across saves. The ring needs its lava hearth but no FE.
guide.arcana_industry.foundry_ring.page2: Right-click the controller with eight batches of a recipe's input. All eight batches load into the controller together; after 40 ticks, right-click with an empty hand to collect the eight results. A busy controller refuses another heat without consuming it. Most recipes take one item per batch; the polished-stone, deepslate-brick and raw-metal recipes take four items for five results, so a heat uses 32 and returns 40. Silk-touched ores yield more than a furnace: diamond and nether quartz ore give 2, redstone ore 5 and lapis ore 6 each. Cobblestone, clay and the stone, nether and blackstone brick recipes stay one-for-one because crushing, polishing or brick reclaiming can reverse them. Breaking a furnace, hearth lining, hood vent, copper heat sink or empty slag cup, or removing the source lava, stops production. Restore the missing part to resume.
guide.arcana_industry.lattice_welder.pag: Craft with a Prism Core, Prism Separator, three sealed steel plates, glass panes, a hopper and one Servo Motor. The servo is the manipulator's position-controlled axis: craft it from a Rotary Encoder on top (feedback), two Stator Coils beside a Magnetized Core rotor, a Deep Groove Ball Bearing below and four sealed steel plates as the housing. A plain Wound Motor has no encoder and cannot replace it. This machine is available alongside the Lattice Scriber.

Insert material from the top or horizontal faces; extract results below. Configure side modes in the GUI. Provide 22 FE/t or use the crank. A full output pauses work; stored items, FE and progress survive chunk reload.

Weld two Sealed Steel Plates edge-to-edge into one Welded Plate, required in the Lattice Laminator craft. A single plate cannot start this operation. Twenty-two tagged metal recipes fabricate vanilla metal goods from mod ingots instead of iron, gold or copper, so these ores keep a use after their own tier: 2 cobalt -> shears, 4 iridium -> blast furnace, 3 manganese -> 8 rails, 3 bismuth -> bucket, 7 gallium -> cauldron, 6 thallium -> 16 iron bars, 2 antimony -> 2 chains, 2 palladium -> light and 2 rhodium -> heavy weighted pressure plate, 6 ruthenium -> 3 iron doors, 4 tantalum -> iron trapdoor, 5 zirconium -> minecart, 3 germanium -> lightning rod, 2 hafnium -> shield, 2 indium -> 2 lanterns, 2 molybdenum -> flint and steel, 5 niobium -> hopper, 24 osmium -> anvil, 4 platinum -> clock, 3 rhenium -> stonecutter, 2 titanium -> smithing table, 1 tungsten -> 2 tripwire hooks. Storage blocks are packed by the Compaction Spire or a crafting table, not here. JEI lists input, output, duration, FE and priority.

Rated Pressure Shell (seam welding): craft a Pressure Shell Blank from one Stainless Vessel Stock (Kiln) between two Flanged Rings (Flange Press) as the dished heads, then weld one blank for 240 ticks at 26 FE/t. The circumferential seams join the heads to the barrel and make a closed shell rated for pressure; the Phase Sublimator craft needs it. A plain sealed plate or the unwelded blank cannot replace the shell. Hoppers can feed blanks from the top and pull shells from the bottom like any other welding recipe.
guide.arcana_industry.lattice_engraver.p: Craft with a Prism Core, Prism Separator, Scribed Plate, three sealed steel plates, a hopper and a Programmed Logic Controller (middle right). The Scribed Plate and the controller both come from the Lattice Scriber and gate this t8 apparatus; a glass pane or an unscribed Logic Board Blank no longer fits the controller slot. Material update: crafting slot 4 (row-major 3x3) now requires a ruthenium ingot via forge:ingots/ruthenium; all existing progression gates remain required.
Feed a Prism Core to engrave an Etched Prism (120 ticks, 20 FE/t). The Etched Prism replaces the bottom-right plate in the Stasis Weaver craft and is its sole recipe producer.

Nineteen other recipes shape useful building and circuit substrates. Three tagged metal recipes engrave 2 indium ingots into a lantern, 2 osmium ingots into a heavy weighted pressure plate and 5 palladium ingots into a cauldron (160 ticks, 24 FE/t each). Stone, stone bricks, nether bricks, polished blackstone, purpur and red sandstone are engraved four at a time into five shaped blocks, beating the stonecutter. JEI lists inputs, outputs, time, power and priority. Datapacks use arcana_industry:lattice_engraving; highest priority wins, then recipe ID.

Top and horizontal faces import, bottom exports. Configure each face in the menu. FE capability or crank powers work. A full output pauses processing; inventory, FE, progress and sides persist. Breaking drops stored items.
guide.arcana_industry.stasis_weaver.page: Craft a Stasis Weaver with a Prism Core, Collimated Lens, Etched Prism from a Lattice Engraver, sealed steel plates, glass panes and a hopper. This t8 apparatus precedes the Containment Forge.
Feed an item into the left slot and supply 20 FE/t for 80 ticks (120 for a Phase Lattice). A Phase Lattice yields a Stasis Core, needed in the bottom-right Containment Forge craft corner.

Nineteen other stasis weaving recipes compact distinct materials into usable blocks or components. Five gunpowder weave into one TNT, the same five an Ash Bellows recovers, so the pair never gains powder. JEI lists input counts, output, work time, FE and priority. Datapacks use arcana_industry:stasis_weaving; higher priority wins, then recipe ID.

Stasis compacts, it never invents: the product's material traits must fit inside the combined traits of the consumed inputs (count x input). Four glowstone dust (luminous 2 each) hold the glow of a glowstone block, and four nautilus shells add up to the sea power of a heart of the sea. A datapack row that would add a trait, such as packing untraited snowballs into a fiery magma block, halts with "Product traits not in input or field" before spending FE and keeps its input.

Top and horizontal faces import; bottom exports. Configure faces through menu buttons. FE capability or crank charges the machine. Work pauses on a full output slot; inventory, FE, work and side modes persist. Breaking the block drops its slots.
guide.arcana_industry.phase_conflux.page: The tenth and final t9 apparatus. Craft it with one each of Modulated Phase, Stabilized Phase, Preserved Phase and Effused Phase, two glass panes, a hopper, a sealed steel plate and a Phase Effuser -- a four-way convergence that finally consumes all four leaf materials the Modulator, Stabilizer, Preserver and Effuser reserved for this recipe.

Feed one item into the left slot. The conflux spends 20 FE/t for 150 ticks and yields a single sealed result in the right slot; like the other t9 units there is no second byproduct channel. Confluxing two Effused Phase yields the Converged Phase, the capstone t9 material.

Twenty datapack recipes. Fifteen converge two concrete powders of one color into that color's glazed terracotta, a clay-free sand-and-gravel glaze route no furnace offers (white powder carries no pigment, so it has no row). Four recover two dye from yellow, lime, pink or brown glazed terracotta; brown otherwise needs jungle cocoa. Confluence obeys the material-trait rule with no field: a product may only carry the traits of count x its input. Two concrete powders (rigid 1, pigment 1 each) cover glazed terracotta's rigid 2 and pigment 2, a glaze sheds its pigment as dye, and two Effused Phase (luminous 1, resonant 1 each) cover the Converged Phase's luminous 2 and resonant 2. A datapack row whose product needs other traits, such as glazing terracotta into amethyst, pauses on status "unexplained_traits" without spending FE. JEI displays the result and FE. Recipe type arcana_industry:confluence accepts ingredient, count, result, duration, energy_per_tick and optional priority. Higher priority wins; equal priority uses recipe ID.

Top and horizontal sides import; bottom exports the result. Side mode buttons configure each face. Supply FE by capability or manual crank. The machine pauses if the output slot is full; inventory, FE, work progress and side modes persist. Breaking it drops both slots. Two Converged Phase feed the Phase Heart rite at an Astral Font, the last step before the Phase Scepter capstone.
guide.arcana_industry.phase_modulator.pa: A sixth t9 apparatus. Craft it with an Inverted Phase, four sealed steel plates, two glass panes, a hopper and a Phase Inverter. Material update: crafting slot 4 (row-major 3x3) now requires a thallium ingot via forge:ingots/thallium; all existing progression gates remain required.

Feed one item into the left slot. The modulator spends 20 FE/t for 150 ticks and yields a single sealed result in the right slot; like the other t9 units there is no second byproduct channel. Modulating two Inverted Phase yields the Modulated Phase, reserved for a future t9 convergence recipe.

Twenty datapack recipes cover copper, deepslate, blackstone, nether and ice/prismarine reprocessing into dense or rarer alternate forms. Modulation obeys the material-trait rule with no field: a product may only carry the traits of count x its input, so a material is re-formed only inside its own family. Every copper form keeps the ingot signature (flexible 1, heavy 1), deepslate forms heavy 2 and rigid 1, basalt and blackstone forms heavy 1 and fiery 1, prismarine masonry aqueous 1 and crystalline 1, soul soil and sand umbral 1; ice thins as it unpacks (blue aqueous 3/crystalline 2, packed 2/1, ice 1/1), nylium and magma give up their heat to netherrack (fiery 1), a sea lantern breaks into prismarine crystals, and two Inverted Phase (luminous 1, resonant 1 each) cover the Modulated Phase. A datapack row whose product needs other traits, such as ice becoming magma or one ice becoming blue ice, pauses on status "unexplained_traits" without spending FE. JEI displays the result and FE. Recipe type arcana_industry:modulation accepts ingredient, count, result, duration, energy_per_tick and optional priority. Higher priority wins; equal priority uses recipe ID. Prismarine bricks modulate 4 -> 2 dark prismarine, because milling recovers eight shards from each dark block; this keeps the shard loop non-gaining. Chiseled polished blackstone modulates 1 -> 1 polished blackstone brick, matching the 4 -> 4 Resonance Basin cut so the pair cannot multiply bricks. One blue ice modulates into nine packed ice, matching the Compaction Spire's nine packed ice per blue ice.

Top and horizontal sides import; bottom exports the result. Side mode buttons configure each face. Supply FE by capability or manual crank. The machine pauses if the output slot is full; inventory, FE, work progress and side modes persist. Breaking it drops both slots.
guide.arcana_industry.phase_stabilizer.p: A seventh t9 apparatus. Craft it with a Modulated Phase, four sealed steel plates, two glass panes, a hopper and a Phase Modulator. Material update: crafting slot 4 (row-major 3x3) now requires a hafnium ingot via forge:ingots/hafnium; all existing progression gates remain required.

Feed one item into the left slot. The stabilizer spends 20 FE/t for 150 ticks and yields a single sealed result in the right slot; like the other t9 units there is no second byproduct channel. Stabilizing two Modulated Phase yields the Stabilized Phase; two Stabilized Phase feed the Phase Preserver, which returns a Preserved Phase.

Twenty datapack recipes reclaim redstone, iron and copper from functional contraptions (observer, dispenser, dropper, piston), or recover six oak planks from a note block. Each yield is at or below the crafting cost: an observer returns 2 redstone, a dispenser or dropper 1, and the note block six of eight planks. A smoker is stripped back to its furnace. Other recipes exchange crafting stations and lighting blocks for related forms. Stabilization obeys the material-trait rule with no field: a product may only carry the traits of count x its input. Observer, dispenser and dropper keep their dust's signature (resonant 2, luminous 1) to cover redstone; piston and smithing table carry their iron (rigid 2, heavy 2), the lightning rod its copper (heavy 1), and the loom its string; a sticky piston carries only its piston's traits (an Astral Relay makes one from two pistons without slime), so the stabilizer unsticks it back into a piston rather than yielding slime; two Modulated Phase (luminous 1, resonant 1 each) cover the Stabilized Phase. A datapack row whose product needs other traits, such as a loom returning redstone, pauses on status "unexplained_traits" without spending FE. JEI displays the result and FE. Recipe type arcana_industry:stabilization accepts ingredient, count, result, duration, energy_per_tick and optional priority. Higher priority wins; equal priority uses recipe ID.

Top and horizontal sides import; bottom exports the result. Side mode buttons configure each face. Supply FE by capability or manual crank. The machine pauses if the output slot is full; inventory, FE, work progress and side modes persist. Breaking it drops both slots.
guide.arcana_industry.phase_preserver.pa: An eighth t9 apparatus. Craft it with a Stabilized Phase, four sealed steel plates, two glass panes, a hopper and a Phase Stabilizer.

Feed one item into the left slot. The preserver spends 20 FE/t for 150 ticks and yields a single sealed result in the right slot; like the other t9 units there is no second byproduct channel. Preserving two Stabilized Phase yields the Preserved Phase, which the Phase Effuser releases as the Effused Phase.

Twenty datapack recipes reclaim base ingredients from prepared food (bread, cake, cookie, baked potato, pumpkin pie, golden apple, golden carrot) and cooked dishes (cooked beef, porkchop, mutton, chicken, rabbit, cod, salmon, honey bottle, suspicious stew, rabbit stew, mushroom stew, beetroot soup). The three stews return their bowl; beetroot soup instead recovers two of its six beetroot, a useful dye and soup input. Preservation obeys the material-trait rule with no field: a product may only carry the traits of count x its input. Beef and porkchop keep their hide (flexible 2, as leather), chicken its plumage (buoyant 2, flexible 1, as a feather) and rabbit its pelt (flexible 1, buoyant 1), raw or cooked; two Stabilized Phase (luminous 1, resonant 1 each) cover the Preserved Phase. A datapack row whose product needs other traits, such as cooked beef returning a feather, pauses on status "unexplained_traits" without spending FE. JEI displays the result and FE. Recipe type arcana_industry:preservation accepts ingredient, count, result, duration, energy_per_tick and optional priority. Higher priority wins; equal priority uses recipe ID.
