Import from top and horizontal faces; export below. Set side Off/In/Out modes in the menu. Supply 20 FE/t or crank manually. Work takes 160 ticks and pauses when the output is full. Inventory, energy, progress and modes persist.

Datapacks add arcana_industry:photolysis recipes with ingredient, count, result, duration, energy_per_tick and optional priority. Higher priority wins; ID breaks ties. JEI shows the recipes and Photolyzer catalyst.
guide.arcana_industry.spectral_filter.pa: Craft this t7 apparatus with three sealed steel plates, a Faceted Prism Seal, a Coated Interference Filter, two glass panes, a hopper and a Prism Separator. The seal comes only from the Prism Lapidary. Make the filter by crafting a Filter Window Blank from two glass panes around quartz, then coating it with one hafnium ingot in the Silvering Bath; plain quartz or the uncoated blank no longer completes the craft. The film's band selection is abstracted. This is a plain FE machine. Material update: crafting slot 4 (row-major 3x3) now requires a rhodium ingot via forge:ingots/rhodium; all existing progression gates remain required.

Twenty datapack filtration recipes refine light-adjacent minerals: quartz, amethyst, redstone, lapis and prismarine components convert back and forth, and their blocks break down into the loose form. JEI shows the ingredient, FE per tick, output space and priority. Recipe type: arcana_industry:filtration; fields ingredient, count, result, duration, energy_per_tick and optional priority.

The very first recipe filters a Prism Core into a Filtered Prism, a part with no other source. The Lens Collimator now needs one Filtered Prism in place of its first sealed steel plate corner: a bare plate there no longer completes that craft, so the Spectral Filter must be built before the Lens Collimator.

Top and horizontal faces import; bottom exports. Each side is configurable in the GUI. Supply 16 FE/t or use the manual crank. Inventory, FE, progress and port modes persist; breaking drops inventory.
guide.arcana_industry.spectral_loom.page: Craft this t6 controller with two Refracted Matrix, two white wool, a loom, a Solenoid in the centre, a Solar Prism etched in the Heliostat Etcher and two Coil Springs in the bottom corners. The Solenoid is the hook-selection actuator, as electronic Jacquard heads lift each warp hook with a short-stroke electromagnet; a scaffolding block, a bare Soft-Iron Plunger or a loose Wound Coil cannot replace it. Make it from four iron ingots (the magnetic C-frame), a Wound Coil from the Induction Coiler, a Soft-Iron Plunger and a Coil Spring that returns the plunger when the coil is off. For the plunger, draw one tagged iron ingot into a Drawn Iron Rod on the Wire Drawing Bench, then anneal it in the Induction Coiler: cold drawing hardens iron, and annealing makes it magnetically soft again so the plunger releases cleanly. Pull force, stroke, duty cycle and coil heating are not simulated. The springs return the heddle treadles after each pick, as real loom treadles are sprung back; wool cannot replace them. Draw them on the Wire Drawing Bench: one Tool Steel Stock gives four springs. Real springs are cold-coiled from hardened, drawn wire and then stress relieved at about 200-315 C to remove coiling stress; the bench abstracts coiling, stress relief and spring rate. The prism commits the textile branch to t6 before its Woven Sigil is bound in a Reliquary Stand, sealed at a Concordance Altar, and keyed in an Iridescent Basin.

Place a loom below, a scaffolding block above, white wool north and south, and cobwebs east and west, then lay a stripped oak log warp beam on top of each cobweb. All eight parts must remain in place. Right-click with a full input batch; breaking any arm stops production.

Sixteen dye batches weave each vanilla dye directly into eight blocks of matching colored wool, skipping the usual wool cost. Sixteen more batches weave four colored wool into eight matching colored carpet. A fusion batch compresses two Refracted Matrix into a Lumen Filament for the next t5 controller.

Right-click with a full batch for direct hand feeding. For automation, insert recipe inputs through the top or horizontal controller faces and extract finished textiles from the bottom; each port exposes one slot. The two-slot buffer persists through save/load and drops its contents if broken. Processing pauses when any frame block is missing or output is full. No FE or fluid port is needed. JEI shows loaded batches; matching ties resolve by resource ID.
guide.arcana_industry.twin_channel_washe: Craft the controller with sealed steel plate, water buckets, copper ingots and iron bars. Set it over stone bricks. Place copper blocks east and west, iron bars at the four level diagonal corners, and source water above both the north and south adjacent spaces. Extend two blocks east and west from the controller with a hopper at each end and a stone-brick support directly below each hopper.

Right-click the formed washer holding a complete matching batch to load one arcana_industry:channel_washing recipe. The controller finishes it after 40 ticks; collect the buffered result with an empty hand. Gravel yields flint, sand yields clay balls, cobblestone wears to gravel and soul sand rinses to soul soil. Missing either source, the bed, a copper bank, an iron brace or a supported settling hopper stops processing without consuming items.

Four raw gold washed together concentrate into one Panned Concentrate. Two concentrate craft the Rotary Screen, whose Screened Silica is required for the Electrolyzer. The washer uses its own datapack recipe type exclusively; ordinary Ore Sluice sluicing recipes do not run here. The two end hoppers are required settling drains; they do not feed the controller. Feed it with a separate hopper or pipe on the controller as described below.

Soil batches: coarse dirt rinses to dirt, rooted dirt releases hanging roots, dirt hydrates into mud, mud settles into clay, and packed mud softens back to mud. Four bricks blocks reclaim sixteen clay balls, matching sixteen clay balls annealed into brick items and pressed into those blocks; four terracotta rinse into eight reusable brick items; clay blocks break into clay balls. Feed four of the named input item for each batch.

Recovery batches: rinse prismarine into shards, sea lanterns into crystals, glowstone into dust, magma blocks into magma cream, red mushroom blocks into mushrooms, cobwebs into string and oak leaves into sticks. These recipes reclaim materials from built or gathered blocks. All 20 channel_washing recipes are data-pack entries. Hand feeding and port automation both work; a full input buffer refuses another hand-fed batch without taking it.
Four sea lanterns rinse into twenty prismarine crystals (five per lantern). Crystal-to-lantern machines require at least five crystals per lantern, so recovery cannot multiply the input.

For automation, insert valid channel_washing stock into the controller from any face except the bottom and extract products from the bottom. Each formed batch takes 40 ticks; a missing water source, bed, copper bank, iron brace or settling hopper pauses processing without consuming stock. The controller buffers one input stack and one output stack, saves both and its face modes, and exposes Forge item handlers to hoppers or pipes; stock with no matching recipe is refused. Sneak-right-click with an empty hand to cycle the clicked face through input, output and disabled; right-click with an empty hand to collect buffered output. It has no FE or fluid port. Matching ties resolve by resource ID.
guide.arcana_industry.heraldic_frame.pag: Craft this seventh t6 controller with two Lumen Filament from the Spectral Loom, four oak planks, two white banners, and a red wool block. The filament is the progression gate.

Place a red wool block below, an oak fence above, oak planks two blocks north and south, and white banners east and west. Top the oak fence with a second oak fence and a spruce plank crossbar reaching over both banners. All nine parts must remain in place. Right-click with a full input batch; breaking any arm stops production.

Sixteen dye batches weave each vanilla dye directly into a matching colored banner, skipping the usual wool-and-stick cost. Sixteen more batches weave four colored carpet into a matching colored bed. A fusion batch compresses two Lumen Filament into a Woven Sigil for the next t5 controller.

Right-click while holding a full batch to load it into the frame; a second hand batch is refused until the first finishes. Collect the product with an empty hand after processing. For automation, face a hopper or pipe into the open north side and extract finished goods from the open south side. Sneak-right-click an empty hand on a face to cycle input, output or disabled. A formed frame processes one buffered batch every 40 ticks; stored stock and output survive reload. Hand feeding still works. JEI shows every loaded batch; matching ties resolve by resource ID.
guide.arcana_industry.material_traits.pa: Arcane crafting does not invent properties; it carries them. Every material has traits with a strength from 1 to 5. Examples: woven (string, banners, sigils), pigment (dyes), waxen and luminous (candles), resonant and crystalline (amethyst), buoyant (feathers), rigid and heavy (iron), fiery (blaze), aqueous (water).

Inheritance rule: the strengths of all inputs add up, to a maximum of 5. A product may hold only traits that some input carried, and never more strongly than the inputs combined. A dyed banner is woven from the white banner plus pigment from the dye. A Concordance Seal is binding from the Reliquary Core plus resonant and crystalline from amethyst. Stone plus wood can never make light.

Metal grit carries half of its ingot's traits: dense metal grit is rigid 1 and heavy 1, aluminum grit only rigid 1. That is why Reliquary Binding needs two grits for each ingot (rigid 2, heavy 2; aluminum and titanium ingots are rigid 2 only). Two Woven Sigils (woven 4, binding 4) likewise cover the Reliquary Core's binding 3 and woven 1. Confluence glazes inherit the same way.

Some traits oppose each other: fiery/aqueous, buoyant/heavy, rigid/flexible, rigid/waxen, crystalline/flexible and luminous/umbral. A pool holding opposed traits is unstable. Instability = for each opposed pair, the weaker side's strength, plus 1 for every distinct trait beyond four (complex fusions are harder). Feather plus iron scores 3: buoyant 2 against heavy 2, rigid 2 against flexible 1.

Stabilising a rite: a Concordance Altar holds instability 1 on its own, plus 1 for each amethyst block on its four diagonal corners at altar height. A corner Astral Font holding at least 100 lumen adds 2 instead; when a fusion needs more than the altar and amethyst hold, it spends 100 lumen from each font it leans on (in fixed corner order). A backlash costs no lumen. Lumen cannot be made industrially, so harder fusions are paid for with starlight. If a fusion's instability is higher, it backlashes: the off-hand reagent is spent, the main-hand base is kept, and the player takes 2 magic damage per point of excess. Quenched Obsidian (water bucket + 2 blaze powder -> 2 obsidian, the bucket is returned) scores 3, so it needs two corner amethyst blocks. Automation note: altar fusions are hand rites; use the assay first.

Assay at a formed Concordance Altar: use it while holding one item, or a pair with no fusion recipe. The altar consumes nothing. Instead it lists each item's traits, the pool a fusion would inherit, and the number of opposed pairs (green = stable, red = unstable), then the instability score against this altar's stability. The altar also enforces the rule: if a recipe, including one added by a datapack, would give a product a trait that its inputs lack, the altar refuses and names the missing trait.

Datapacks can add traits in data/<namespace>/arcana_traits/traits/<id>.json, with an "opposes" list. Assign them in arcana_traits/materials/<id>.json, using "items" and/or "tags" plus a "traits" map of strengths. Reloading applies changes. Unknown traits or items, strengths outside 1..5 and malformed files are skipped with a log warning instead of breaking the pack. Every Concordance Altar recipe is audited against this rule.
guide.arcana_industry.power_cables.page1: Cables carry Forge Energy (FE) from any block that lets energy be extracted, such as this mod's Firebox Dynamo or another mod's generator or battery, into machines that accept it. Craft them on a crafting table: Tin Wire from three tin ingots (forge:ingots/tin) in a row, 6 wires. Copper Cable from three copper ingots between two rows of Carded Fiber, 6 cables. Silver Cable from silver ingots between Porcelain Insulators, 6. Aluminum Cable from aluminum ingots between Green Porcelain Insulators, 6. Niobium Line from five niobium ingots and four Green Porcelain Insulators, 4.
guide.arcana_industry.power_cables.page2: Each cable has a voltage class and current rating: Tin Wire 16 V x 2 A (32 FE/t, 400 mOhm per block), Copper 64 V x 4 A (256 FE/t, 160 mOhm), Silver 256 V x 4 A (1024 FE/t, 60 mOhm), Aluminum 1024 V x 8 A (8192 FE/t, 110 mOhm), Niobium 4096 V x 16 A (65536 FE/t, 5 mOhm). A run never moves more than its rating. Every delivery pays resistive I^2R loss that grows with the number of cable blocks crossed, so a long low-voltage run wastes power; a run long enough to drop its whole voltage (20 tin wires carrying the full 2 A) delivers nothing.
guide.arcana_industry.power_cables.page3: Condition: only cables of the same kind join; a copper cable beside a silver cable stays open, so each run keeps one voltage class. A generator that declares a class, such as the Trickle (16 V) Firebox Dynamo, only feeds a run of that class: touching a lower-class cable burns that cable (overvoltage, no drop), and a higher-class run takes nothing from it (undervoltage). Generators from other mods declare no class and feed any run. A cable face joins a neighbouring cable or any block with an energy port. Right-click a face with an empty hand to switch it off; the face stays off after saving and reloading the world, and switching it again re-links it. Cables store no energy, so breaking one loses nothing.
guide.arcana_industry.power_cables.page4: Automation: a cable touching an extractable energy holder pulls from it every 10 ticks (half a second) and feeds the receivers on its run nearest first, simulating each transfer before taking energy. Use switched-off faces as side configuration: turn off the face against a machine that should not be fed, or the face against a battery the run must not drain. Machines in this mod accept FE but never give it back, so a run from a generator through several machines fills the closest ones first.
guide.arcana_industry.power_cables.page5: Transformers join two neighbouring classes: Trickle-Low Transformer (16/64 V), Low-Medium Transformer (64/256 V), Medium-High Transformer (256/1024 V) and High-Surge Transformer (1024/4096 V). Craft each on a crafting table around a Laminated Transformer Core: the lower class's cable on the top and left, the higher class's cable on the right and bottom, and four ingots of the higher conductor's metal in the corners (copper, silver, aluminum, niobium). Mine with a pickaxe; it drops itself.
guide.arcana_industry.power_cables.page6: Use: the face pointing at you when placed is the high-voltage terminal (white or coloured insulator); the other five faces are the low-voltage terminal. Right-click with an empty hand to switch Step up (lamp chevron rising: low faces in, front out) or Step down (chevron falling: front in, low faces out). A transformer keeps no buffer: a run that reaches its input terminal at the input class carries on through it into the output run in the same push, at 96% efficiency, plus both runs' line loss. A run of the wrong class is refused, never converted.
guide.arcana_industry.power_cables.page7: Why step up: the same power at four times the voltage needs a quarter of the current and loses a sixteenth as much. Example: Firebox Dynamos on short Tin Wire into a Trickle-Low transformer, a long Copper Cable trunk, then a Low-Trickle step-down (another Trickle-Low transformer set to Step down) beside the machines. Automation: transformers are passive, so the trunk works whenever a generator runs; switch a cable face off to isolate a branch. At most four transformers can be chained in one push.
guide.arcana_industry.power_cables.page8: Machine voltage classes: every machine takes power only at the class of its tier, two tiers per class: Tier 0-1 Trickle (16 V), Tier 2-3 Low (64 V), Tier 4-5 Medium (256 V), Tier 6-7 High (1024 V), Tier 8-9 Surge (4096 V). A run of a lower class leaves the machine idle; a run of a higher class burns the cable touching the machine (no drop) and stops that push, so step the line down first. The Strata Excavator is Low, and the powered Arc Press and Induction Coiler frames are Medium: a Stock Hatch linked to their controller takes power at the controller's class, while an unlinked hatch takes nothing. The Firebox Dynamo feeds only Trickle machines it touches directly. Another mod's cables and generators skip this check. Datapacks can move a machine with the block tags arcana_industry:load_class/<class>.
guide.arcana_industry.power_cables.page9: Datapack ratings: data/arcana_industry/arcana_conductors/<cable>.json sets rated_current (1-64 A) and milliohms_per_block (0-10000) for tin_wire, copper_cable, silver_cable, aluminum_cable or niobium_line, and applies on /reload. The voltage class cannot change. Invalid or unknown files are ignored with a log warning and the values above stay.
guide.arcana_industry.stock_hatch.page1: Craft two Stock Hatches from four tin ingots (forge:ingots/tin), two zinc ingots (forge:ingots/zinc), a hopper and a redstone dust. A hatch is a frame part, not a machine: it has no recipes of its own and needs no FE or lumen.
guide.arcana_industry.stock_hatch.page2: Twelve stock-fed frames enclose their controller on all six faces: Arc Press, Armor Delaminator, Capacitor Array, Chromatic Kiln, Degauss Coil, Flux Rectifier, Induction Coiler, Magnetizer, Milling Gantry, Polarity Inverter, Signal Imprinter and Soaking Hearth. Place a hatch instead of any part that touches the controller face-to-face; the frame still forms with up to two hatches and must not have a third. Corner and outer parts cannot be replaced.
guide.arcana_industry.stock_hatch.page3: Automation: a hatch exposes a Forge item handler on every face that relays the controller face it covers, using that face's In/Out/Off mode. Hoppers, droppers and item pipes insert stock through a hatch on an In face, simulated inserts change nothing, and products are extracted from a hatch on an Out face (the base face starts as Out). Sneak-use a hatch with an empty hand to cycle the covered face; right-click it with an empty hand to collect products.
guide.arcana_industry.stock_hatch.page4: A hatch only relays while it touches exactly one formed controller; removing the hatch, the controller or any frame part closes the port and the controller keeps its saved buffers. Hatches hold no items themselves, so breaking one never drops stock.
guide.arcana_industry.structure_projecto: Craft it from two amethyst shards and a glass pane over two copper ingots and redstone dust, with a third copper ingot below (ingots by forge:ingots/copper, the pane by forge:glass_panes). The amethyst lens and copper body make it usable from the start, before your first multiblock.

Place a multiblock controller first, then right-click it with the projector. Clicking a block without a blueprint clears the previous projection, so rebind it to a controller at your new site. Breaking the bound controller hides its hologram; right-click in the air to clear that stale binding. While you hold the projector, each missing part is drawn in place as a faint, shrunken copy of the block it needs, inside a cyan frame. A red frame marks a position that holds the wrong block. Parts that are already correct disappear from the projection, and the action bar shows how many are still missing.

Right-click in the air to step through the layers. It shows all layers, then each layer from the bottom up, then all layers again, so you can build one level at a time without the upper layers hiding the lower ones. Sneak and right-click in the air to turn the projection off. The projector never places or removes blocks itself.

The shapes come from datapack blueprints at data/<namespace>/multiblocks/<controller>.json, a list of parts with right, up and forward offsets (right is east and forward is north of the controller) and a block state such as minecraft:piston[facing=west]. Adding [source] to a fluid block requires a still source. A datapack can add a blueprint for a new controller or override one of ours. Invalid files are skipped with a log warning. The controller's own check decides formation; the projection is only a building guide.
guide.arcana_industry.ore_mite.page1: Ore Mites gather in dripstone and lush caves. Their amethyst-striped backs distinguish them from common silverfish. They are hostile cave ambushers; a successful bite causes Hunger for five seconds. Bring food and keep the mining route lit.
guide.arcana_industry.ore_mite.page2: Defeating an Ore Mite always yields one amethyst shard. Combine a shard with a prism core in the t8 Lattice Composer to make phase lattice, then use the lattice to craft the t9 Phase Annealer. The mite offers a renewable cave source of this progression ingredient.
guide.arcana_industry.ore_mite.page3: An Ore Mite killed by a Static Creeper blast also drops the Vein Echo music disc. Lure a creeper into a swamp cave where mites can spawn, then draw the mite into the blast; an ordinary kill does not yield the disc. Its five-beat cave melody plays in any jukebox, and its comparator output of 11 distinguishes it from Lattice Hymn and Corroded Waltz.
guide.arcana_industry.ore_mite.page4: Rare trophy: when a player lands the killing blow, an Ore Mite sometimes also drops a Mite Chitin scale (35% base, +10% per Looting level). The chitin is found only on this mob. Crush it in the Crusher for three amethyst shards, which feed phase-lattice and vitrified amethyst work long before geodes are found.
guide.arcana_industry.provision_hearth.p: Craft the controller from sealed steel plates, bricks and a smoker. Set it directly above a lit campfire. Put a smoker on each diagonal corner at controller height to form a raised X around it.

Right-click the formed controller with four times a hearth recipe's input count to load one four-smoker heat. The held stack loses only that amount; the controller smokes it over 40 ticks and produces four results. A second hand-fed heat is refused while stock or output waits, without taking items. Right-click with an empty hand to collect the finished food, or extract it from a configured output side. Extinguishing the campfire or removing any smoker pauses processing without consuming the loaded stock.

Twenty-one exclusive arcana_industry:hearth_smoking recipes cure trail rations, fuel and a t3 gate material: four raw beef, chicken, porkchop, mutton, rabbit, cod, salmon or kelp into five cooked or dried pieces (the slow smoke wastes less than a smoker); one potato into one baked potato; one spider eye into one fermented spider eye (the Condenser reverses two for two); sugar cane into sugar; nine wheat into four loaves of bread; nine dried kelp into a dried kelp block; honeycomb into a honey bottle; four birch, spruce, acacia or dark oak logs into five charcoal; four chorus fruit into five popped chorus fruit for End building; two rotten flesh into one smoke-cured leather, a drop sink for zombie farms; and leather into Cured Lashing, a smoke-tanned cord needed once for the Leaching Vat craft and once for an Electrolyzer corner.

This recipe type is exclusive to the Provision Hearth and separate from vanilla minecraft:smoking, so other mods' or vanilla's furnace-smoker recipes do not apply here. JEI lists its hearth smoking recipes under the Provision Hearth catalyst, with the quadrupled input and four separate output stacks shown. For automation, a hopper above the controller or a compatible pipe inserts recipe stock into a buffered input slot; the hearth waits until four batches are present, then smokes them in 40 ticks into four results. The lit campfire fills the bottom face, so sneak-right-click a free side with an empty hand to cycle it from input to output (then disabled) and pull products with a pipe or other Forge item handler; right-click with an empty hand to collect them yourself. Unmatched stock is refused, a missing smoker or unlit campfire pauses work without consuming stock, and both buffers and face modes are saved. It has no FE or fluid port.
guide.arcana_industry.quern.page1: Build a quern from four cobblestone, two iron ingots and three oak planks. Crafting rows: cobblestone/iron/cobblestone; plank/plank/plank; cobblestone/iron/cobblestone. Mine it with a stone pickaxe or better. This t0 apparatus uses the manual crank and Forge Energy. Mill two wheat into Ground Meal for the kiln's top-right slot; a plain brick cannot replace it. This Industry Field Guide itself is crafted shapeless from one book and one cobblestone.
guide.arcana_industry.quern.page2: Right-click to open the quern. It reuses the crusher's menu layout: place material in the left slot, collect meal from the right slot, Crank supplies 80 FE, and six buttons cycle each world face through Off, In and Out exactly like the crusher and sieve.
guide.arcana_industry.quern.page3: The quern mills plant and bone material that the crusher and sieve do not process: wheat, seeds, rotten flesh, nether wart, cocoa beans, potatoes, carrots, apples and glow berries each grind into Ground Meal, a general-purpose milled powder. Reserve one Ground Meal for the first kiln; spare meal converts into bone meal at a crafting table.
guide.arcana_industry.quern.page4: The quern also has seventeen specialty outputs: bone yields bone meal directly, sugar cane yields sugar, cactus yields green dye, chorus fruit yields purple dye, shroomlight yields glowstone dust, and brown mushroom, red mushroom, sweet berries, crimson fungus and warped fungus each yield a matching dye. Flowers mill into two dye instead of one: dandelion to yellow, cornflower to blue, lily of the valley to white, oxeye daisy to light gray and allium to magenta. An ink sac gives two black dye and a pumpkin gives four pumpkin seeds. Twenty-nine recipes in total; each has one specific input item.
guide.arcana_industry.quern.page5: Automation: side ports, energy handling, NBT persistence and hopper behavior are identical to the crusher and sieve. This gives farms, mushroom and nether-fungus harvesters a mechanized processing destination alongside crushing and sieving.
guide.arcana_industry.quern.page6: Recipes are datapack JSON under data/<namespace>/recipes/querning. Type: arcana_industry:querning. Fields: ingredient (item or tag), count (default 1), result (item/count), duration (1-72000 ticks), energy_per_tick (1-1000), priority (default 0). Highest priority wins; equal priorities use ascending recipe ID.
guide.arcana_industry.quern.page7: With Just Enough Items installed, click the progress strip to browse Querning recipes, or look up an ingredient or product in JEI. The quern is the category catalyst. JEI is optional; all processing and this guide work without it.
guide.arcana_industry.reliquary_stand.pa: Craft this eighth t6 controller with two Woven Sigil from the Heraldic Frame, four quartz pillars, two gilded blackstone and a soul lantern. The sigil is the progression gate.

Place a netherite block below and a soul lantern above. Put quartz pillars directly east and west, and gilded blackstone two blocks north and two blocks south, each on a polished blackstone brick step. This leaves the north and south faces open. All eight parts must remain in place. Right-click with a full input batch; breaking any arm stops production.

Twenty-three binding batches draw three pure ingots out of two grit of a furnace-smeltable metal, half again the furnace yield and without fire. The six refractory metals (chromium, niobium, tantalum, tungsten, vanadium and zirconium) bind two grit into one ingot, a fuel-free fallback for grit no furnace can melt. A fusion batch compresses two Woven Sigil into a Reliquary Core for the next t5 controller.

Right-click while holding a full batch to load exactly one batch into the stand; it binds over 40 ticks, and an empty-hand right-click collects the product. While a batch is loaded, further hand feeding is refused and consumes nothing. For automation, feed full batches through a hopper or Forge item pipe on the open north face. Sneak-right-click the open south face with an empty hand once to set output, then extract there with a pipe. One input stack and one output stack are buffered; each batch takes 40 ticks while formed and pauses if a part breaks. Another sneak-right-click disables a face, and empty-hand use collects buffered output. No FE or fluids are needed. JEI shows every loaded batch; matching ties resolve by resource ID.
guide.arcana_industry.sanctum_pylon.page: Craft this controller from four amethyst blocks, four sea lanterns and a Vitrified Amethyst, which the Blast Column fuses from four amethyst shards. It is a required t2 structure: one Attuned Starshard is the magical seal in the Leaching Vat craft, so the pylon must be formed before the aqueous tier opens.

Place a lodestone directly below the controller. At the same height as the controller, ring eight sea lanterns around it: one two blocks in each cardinal direction, and one two blocks diagonally at each corner. One block above the controller, place four amethyst blocks at the four cardinal positions. Two blocks above the controller, place a beacon as the capstone.

Right-click the formed pylon holding a full batch matching a loaded arcana_industry:sanctum_attunement recipe. It loads exactly one batch and attunes it for 40 ticks into one trait-imprinted carrier. Amethyst shards, quartz and glowstone dust produce Attuned Starshards for the Leaching Vat seal and other magic crafts. The other seventeen batches recover six useful carriers: prismarine shards from sea offerings, lapis from redstone/lapis/echo offerings, blaze powder from fire offerings, ender pearls from void offerings, leather from animal offerings and glow ink sacs from slime or glow ink. Each return is one item per batch, with its offering trait imprinted; consult JEI for exact input counts. Busy offerings are kept; empty-hand use collects the output.

Attunement keeps one property of the offering. The pylon reads the batch material traits, takes the strongest one (ties go to the lower trait ID), and imprints it on the returned carrier at strength trait x batch size / 2, capped at 5: two ender pearls give Umbral 3 on a returned pearl, while eight lapis give Pigment 5 on returned lapis. An imprinted item carries its trait into trait-aware machines. Differently imprinted carriers do not stack. The Attuned Starshard tooltip names its imprint; other carriers retain their imprint in item data. An offering with no traits is refused and kept.

Breaking the lodestone, any of the eight ring lanterns, any of the four pillar blocks or the capstone beacon stops attunement. Two pylons can share one ring lantern if placed four blocks apart on an axis; only the structurally complete controller may be used, and removing the shared lantern collapses both. JEI shows every loaded batch, and matching ties resolve by resource ID.

For automation, place a hopper in the open space directly above the controller, under the beacon, or run an item pipe into it; it fills the buffered stock slot with offerings that match a loaded batch. Every 40 ticks a formed pylon attunes one complete batch with the same trait imprint as a hand-fed offering; traitless stock waits instead of producing a blank carrier. The lodestone covers the bottom face, so sneak-use the south (or any open side) face once with an empty hand to set it to output and extract carriers there with a pipe. Empty-hand use collects buffered outputs; sneak-use cycles any face between input, output and disabled. Stock and outputs survive saves and chunk reloads, and a broken frame pauses work. The pylon has no FE or fluid port.
guide.arcana_industry.static_creeper.pag: Static Creepers appear in dark swamps and mangrove swamps. At close range they pulse a brief Mining Fatigue charge into their target each second while closing in. They still have a normal creeper fuse and explosion. Keep space between them and workshops, and clear the approach before mining.
A defeated Static Creeper drops two redstone dust. Eight dust can be compressed into a redstone block in the Pressure Press, providing a renewable automation material once the blast risk is managed.

If a Flux Archer's arrow lands the killing shot, the Static Creeper also drops the Lattice Hymn music disc. Lure a Static Creeper into a Flux Archer's line of fire in stony peaks or let the two meet near a swamp edge, then stand clear. The disc plays in any jukebox and outputs comparator strength 9.

Rare trophy: when a player lands the killing blow before the fuse finishes, a Static Creeper sometimes also drops a Static Gland (35% base, +10% per Looting level). The gland is found only on this mob; an exploded creeper leaves nothing. Crush it in the Crusher for five redstone, a strong early supply for circuits and capacitors.
message.arcana_industry.lumen_vessel_too: %s / %s lumen - fill or pour at an Astral Font
jei.arcana_industry.info.strata_excavato: Quarry machine with no recipe category. Each FE-powered dig removes one block from a 9x9 layer below the excavator, working down to the world floor, for 120 FE plus 30 FE per point of block hardness. It holds 64,000 FE; right-click with an empty hand to collect the buffered drops and read power, layer and status.

Sneak-use with an empty hand to toggle ore mode, which skips everything except forge:ores blocks. Air, fluids, block entities, unbreakable blocks and protected blocks (a cancelled break event) are skipped at no cost. A redstone signal pauses digging.

Automation: drops collect in an 18-slot buffer that is pushed every tick into item handlers on the top and four sides, and any item handler or hopper may extract from it. When the buffer is full the machine stops with output_full instead of voiding drops; breaking it spills the buffer.
guide.arcana_industry.strata_excavator.p: Craft the Strata Excavator from four sealed steel plates around a diamond pickaxe (top centre), a Crusher (centre) between two pistons, and a hopper (bottom centre). It is a Tier 3 utility, not a processing machine: it has no recipes of its own. It needs FE from a cable or generator; sneak-use with an empty hand only toggles its mode.

Placed on the surface, it digs the 9x9 area directly below itself, one block every 4 ticks, west to east and north to south, a whole layer at a time, down to the bottom of the world. Each block costs 120 FE plus 30 FE per point of hardness (stone 165 FE, deepslate 210 FE). The 64,000 FE buffer accepts power on every face.

Drops are rolled as if mined with a diamond pickaxe without enchantments, so ores give raw ore and stone gives cobblestone. It leaves air, water, lava, bedrock and anything with a block entity (chests, hoppers, spawners, machines) untouched. Protection mods can veto each break through the normal Forge break event.

Ore mode (sneak-use with an empty hand) only takes blocks in the forge:ores tag, including every Arcana ore, and skips the rest for free, so a shaft through a whole column costs only the ores' FE. Use the block with an empty hand to read FE, current layer, blocks mined, mode and status, and to take the buffered drops.

Automation: the 18-slot buffer pushes one stack per tick into any container or machine on its top or side faces; hoppers and item pipes can also pull from every face, while inserts are refused. A full buffer pauses the dig instead of dropping items. A redstone signal pauses it, unloaded chunks make it wait, and the layer, position, mode, FE and buffer survive saving. Breaking the excavator drops its buffer.
guide.arcana_industry.flux_totem.page1: Craft the Flux Totem from a Phase Heart, four Phase Coils, two Phase Vessels, a Phase Sigil and Ripened Phase. This expensive capstone consumes the vessels and starts empty. The heart requires the 480-lumen Astral Font rite; phase materials require the tier-nine processing chain.
guide.arcana_industry.flux_totem.page2: Sneak-use the totem on the output face of an FE machine to draw up to 8,000 FE per click. Its bar and tooltip show the charge, up to 200,000 FE. The machine must permit extraction from the clicked face. Charge is saved on the item stack.
guide.arcana_industry.flux_totem.page3: Hold a charged totem in either hand. When you would die after ordinary totem protection fails, it spends 100,000 FE and restores one health, regeneration, absorption and fire resistance. It remains in hand and can be recharged. An empty or partly charged totem cannot rescue you. There is no passive effect in inventory.
guide.arcana_industry.flux_totem.page4: Automation: FE generation and cable networks feed the source machine, and a player charges the held totem from its output face. The phase processing line can be stocked with configured item and fluid IO; the Astral Font rite for the heart stays hand-performed.
guide.arcana_industry.flux_aegis.page1: Craft the Flux Aegis from four Phase Lattices, a Phase Coil, two Phase Vessels, Converged Phase and Stabilized Phase. All of them come from the tier-nine phase processing chain, so the aegis is a late reward that starts empty.
guide.arcana_industry.flux_aegis.page2: Sneak-use the aegis on the output face of an FE machine to draw up to 16,000 FE per click. It stores up to 400,000 FE in the item stack, shown by its violet bar and tooltip. The clicked face must permit extraction.
guide.arcana_industry.flux_aegis.page3: Carry a charged aegis anywhere in your inventory. After armor and enchantments reduce a hit, the aegis pays 2,000 FE per health point (one half-heart) instead of your health. When the charge runs short it absorbs what it can, and the rest reaches you. Only the first charged aegis is used. Void damage and /kill are never absorbed.
guide.arcana_industry.flux_aegis.page4: Pair it with a Flux Totem: the aegis spends FE on every hit, and the totem in hand catches the fatal blow once the aegis runs dry. Automation: keep an FE generator and cable network charging a machine buffer, then top up the aegis from its output face between fights.
guide.arcana_industry.flux_lancet.page1: Craft a Flux Lancet from a Phase Heart, Phase Lattice, Phase Coil, Phase Vessel and Converged Phase. These tier-nine components gate the weapon behind the full phase line. It starts uncharged.
guide.arcana_industry.flux_lancet.page2: Sneak-use it on an FE machine's extractable output face to draw up to 12,000 FE per click. It holds 300,000 FE in the stack. The amber bar and tooltip show the remaining charge; the charge persists when the item is saved.
guide.arcana_industry.flux_lancet.page3: Hold it in the main hand and land a direct melee hit. A valid hit spends 4,000 FE to add 12 damage after armor and ordinary damage reduction. This pulse is armor penetrating, but cannot strike an immune target or bypass invulnerability. Empty charge and projectile hits get no pulse. The lancet's ordinary swing remains weak without power.
guide.arcana_industry.flux_lancet.page4: Automation: route FE from a generator through cables into a machine buffer with an extractable face, then charge between fights. Pair it with a carried Flux Aegis for defense and a held Flux Totem for emergency survival.

Astral wand: +50% lumen cost and +25% spell damage per level.
enchantment.arcana_industry.quickcast.de: Astral wand: -25% cooldown and -15% spell damage per level.
enchantment.arcana_industry.thrift.desc: Astral wand: -20% lumen cost and +50% cooldown per level.
guide.arcana_industry.astral_wand.page25: Wands and the Phase Scepter take enchanting-table or anvil-book tunings, each a trade-off up to level III. Overchannel adds 50% lumen cost and 25% damage per level; Quickcast cuts the cooldown 25% but damage 15% per level; Lumen Thrift cuts lumen cost 20% but lengthens the cooldown 50% per level. Tunings exclude each other, so pick one. The tooltip shows the tuned cost, damage and cooldown, and hoppers or Font automation are unaffected.
